translation: And shedding copious tears, he again addressed me, saying, Do you look upon my mother as on your own proud of her son. Having said this, the mighty-armed and illustrious Rāma furnished with eyes resembling lotus-petals, shed plenteous tears.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणस्तु सुसंक्रुद्धो निःश्वसन् वाक्यमब्रवीत्। केनायमपराधेन राजपुत्रो विवासितः॥
translation: Thereupon Lakşmaņa waxing wroth, breathing hard, said, For what fault of his has the Prince been banished?

sanskrit: राज्ञा तु खलु कैकेय्या लघु चाश्रुत्य शासनम्। कृतं कार्यमकार्यं वा वयं येनाभिपीडिताः॥
translation: Observing the worthless command of Kaikeyſ, whether the king has done well or ill, we have been exceedingly pained thereby.

sanskrit: यदि प्रव्राजितो रामो लोभकारणकारितम्। वरदाननिमित्तं वा सर्वथा दुष्कृतं कृतम्॥
translation: Whether Rāma has been exiled through Kaikeyi's lust for dominion or through the exigencies of the bestowal of the boon, there cannot be any doubt that the king has acted most unrighteously.

sanskrit: इदं तावद् यथाकाममीश्वरस्य कृते कृतम्। रामस्य तु परित्यागे न हेतुमुपलक्षये॥
translation: Even if this has been done in harmony with the wish of the Lord, I do not perceive any reason for the banishment of Rāma.

sanskrit: असमीक्ष्य समारब्धं विरुद्धं बुद्धिलाघवात्। जनयिष्यति संक्रोशं राघवस्य विवासनम्॥
translation: The king through lack of sense has done herulessly what is opposed to morality; and this banishment of Rāma will but bring upon him woe here and hereafter.

sanskrit: अहं तावन्महाराजे पितृत्वं नोपलक्षये। भ्राता भर्ता च बन्धुश्च पिता च मम राघवः॥
translation: Fatherhood find I none in the monarch. My brother and feeder and friend and father is even Rāghava.

sanskrit: सर्वलोकप्रियं त्यक्त्वा सर्वलोकहिते रते। सर्वलोकोऽनुरज्येत कथं चानेन कर्मणा॥
translation: Renouncing one that is universally dear, and that is ever engaged in the good of all, how by such an act will the king please the people?

sanskrit: सर्वप्रजाभिरामं हि रामं प्रव्रज्य धार्मिकम्। सर्वलोकविरोधेन कथं राजा भविष्यति ॥
translation: How by banishing the righteous Rāma dear to all the subjects, and thus withstanding the wishes of all, will he retain his royalty?

sanskrit: जानकी तु महाराज निःश्वसन्ती तपस्विनी। भूतोपहतचित्तेव विष्ठिता विस्मृता स्थिता॥
translation: O mighty monarch, Janaki also, unfortunate that she is, sighing heavily, stood wildered like one that had been possessed.

sanskrit: अदृष्टपूर्वव्यसना राजपुत्री यशस्विनी। तेन दुःखेन रुदती नैव मां किंचिदब्रवीत्॥
translation: And not having experienced any calamity before, the famed princes weeping because of this misfortune, told me nothing.

sanskrit: उद्वीक्षमाणा भर्तारं मुखेन परिशिष्यता। मुमोच सहसा बाष्पं प्रयान्तमुपवीक्ष्य सा॥
translation: Looking up to her lord with a blank countenance, she suddenly let fall tears, perceiving the destruction of the subject.

sanskrit: तथैव रामोऽश्रुमुखः कृताञ्जलिः स्थितोऽब्रवील्लक्ष्मणबाहुपालितः। तथैव सीता रुदती तपस्विनी निरीक्षते राजरथं तथैव माम्॥
translation: Thus said Rāma ministered to by Lakşmaņa, with a tearful countenance; and thus stood the unfortunate and weeping Sītå beholding the royal car and myself.

sanskrit: मम त्वश्वा निवृत्तस्य न प्रावर्तन्त वर्त्मनि। उष्णमश्रु विमुञ्चन्तो रामे सम्प्रस्थिते वनम्॥ उभाभ्यां राजपुत्राभ्यामथ कृत्वाहमञ्जलिम्। प्रस्थितो रथमास्थाय तदुःखमपि धारयन्॥
translation: On Rāma having gone to the forest, my horses as I turned away, did not proceed vigorously on the way, and shed warm tears. And having (done homage) to both the princes by joining my hands, I turned my back, bearing as best I could that load of sorrow.

sanskrit: गुहेन सार्धं तत्रैव स्थितोऽस्मि दिवसान् बहून्। आशया यदि मां रामः पुनः शब्दापयेदिति ॥
translation: Indulging in the hope that Rāma might again summon me by any of the envoys (of Guha left there), I stayed there with Guha for many days.

sanskrit: विषये ते महाराज महाव्यसनकर्शिताः। अपि वृक्षाः परिम्लानाः सपुष्पाकुरकोरकाः॥ उपतप्तोदका नद्यः पल्वलानि सरांसि च। परिशुष्कपलाशानि वनान्युपवनानि च॥
translation: In your dominions, O monarch, exercised by the calamity that has befallen Rāma, even trees bearing blossoms and buds and sprouts look sad; the rivers and pools and liquid lapses have their waters dried up; and the woods and groves have their foliage withered.

sanskrit: न च सर्पन्ति सत्त्वानि व्याला न प्रचरन्ति च। रामशोकाभिभूतं त निष्कूजमिव तद्वनम्॥
translation: Creatures do not move and beasts of prey cease to range about; and the forest appears to be dumb, stupefied by grief on account of Rāma.

sanskrit: लीनपुष्करपत्राश्च नद्यश्च कलुषोदकाः। संतप्तपद्माः पद्मिन्यो लीनमीनविहंगमाः॥ जलजानि च पुष्पाणि माल्यानि स्थलजानि च। नातिभान्त्यल्पगन्धीनि फलानि च यथापुरम् ॥
translation: Streams containing lotuses with their leaves shrivelled, have their waters stained; and lotuses have their leaves burnt; and fished and (aquatic) birds have grown lean. And flowers both on land and water have been deprived of their freshness and fragrance; and they no longer retain their former condition.

sanskrit: अत्रोद्यानानि शून्यानि प्रलीनविहगानि च। न चाभिरामानारामान् पश्यामि मनुजर्षभ॥
translation: The gardens are idle with their birds drooping. And, O best of men, I do not find the bowers beautiful (as before).

sanskrit: प्रविशन्तमयोध्यायां न कश्चिदभिनन्दति। नरा राममपश्यन्तो निःश्वसन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः॥
translation: When I entered Ayodhyā, none greeted me. And not seeing Rāma, the people sigh momentarily.

sanskrit: देव राजरथं दृष्ट्वा विना राममिहागतम्। दूरादश्रुमुखः सर्वो राजमार्गे गतो जनः॥
translation: And, O revered one, seeing the royal car returned hither without Rāma, the people on the highways from grief appear with tearful countenance.

sanskrit: हम्र्यैर्विमानैः प्रासादैरवेक्ष्य रथमागतम्। हाहाकारकृता नार्यो रामादर्शनकर्शिताः॥
translation: And from mansions, cars, and lordly edifices, ladies seeing the car come back, set up a chorus of 'Ah' and 'Alas,' afflicted with the absence of Rama.

sanskrit: आयतैर्विमलैनॆत्रैरश्रुवेगपरिप्लुतैः। अन्योन्यमभिवीक्षन्तेऽव्यक्तमार्ततराः स्त्रियः॥
translation: And becoming more distressed that ever, the fair sex with their expansive and clear eyes filled with tears, began to eye each other indistinctly.

sanskrit: नामित्राणां न मित्राणामुदासीनजनस्य च। अहमार्ततया कंचिद् विशेषं नोपलक्षये॥
translation: And in consequence of the general grief that prevailed, I could not perceive any difference between friends and foes and persons indifferent.

sanskrit: अप्रहृष्टमनुष्या च दीननागतुरंगमा। आर्तस्वरपरिम्लानविनिःश्वसितनि:स्वना ॥ निरानन्दा महाराज रामप्रव्राजनातुरा। कौसल्या पुत्रहीनेव अयोध्या प्रतिभाति मे॥
translation: O mighty monarch, distressed in consequence of the exile of Rāma, men appear sunk in dejection, and elephants and horses are spiritless; and seized with cheerlessness, they utter doleful sounds and heave profound sighs. Ayodhyā appears to me joyless like Kausalyă deprived of her son.

sanskrit: सूतस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा वाचा परमदीनया। बाष्पोपहतया सूतमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Hearing the words of the charioteer, the king like an exceedingly forlorn, addressed the former in words lost in the vapour of sorrow.

sanskrit: कैकेय्या विनियुक्तेन पापाभिजनभावया। मया न मन्त्रकुशलैर्वृद्धैः सह समर्थितम्॥
translation: Exhorted by Kaikeyi of a sinful country, born in a sinful race and cherishing sinful designs, I did not take counsel with aged people capable of offering advice.

sanskrit: न सुहृद्भिर्न चामात्यैर्मन्त्रयित्वा सनैगमैः। मयायमर्थः सम्मोहात् स्त्रीहेतोः सहसा कृतः॥
translation: Without consulting with friends or courtiers or persons versed in the Vedas, I have in the interest of a woman rashly done this thing through ignorance.

sanskrit: भवितव्यतया नूनमिदं वा व्यसनं महत्। कुलस्यास्य विनाशाय प्राप्तं सूत यदृच्छया॥
translation: Meseems, O charioteer, for the purpose of destroying this line entirely, this mighty disaster has surely befallen us through the influence of Destiny.

sanskrit: सूत यद्यस्ति ते किंचिन्मयापि सुकृतं कृतम्। त्वं प्रापयाशु मां रामं प्राणाः संत्वरयन्ति माम्॥
translation: O charioteer, if I have ever done you any good do you immediately take me to Rāma: my life urges me on (in this direction).

sanskrit: यद्यद्यापि ममैवाज्ञा निवर्तयतु राघवम्। न शक्ष्यामि विना रामं मुहूर्तमपि जीवितुम्॥
translation: Or let my command make Rāghava turn back. I cannot live for a moment without Rāma.

sanskrit: अथवापि महाबाहुर्गतो दूरं भविष्यति। मामेव रथमारोप्य शीघ्रं रामाय दर्शय॥
translation: But if that mighty-armed one has proceeded far, do you placing me on a car speedily show me to Rāma.

sanskrit: वृत्तदंष्ट्रो महेष्वासः क्वासौ लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः। यदि जीवामि साध्वेनं पश्येयं सीतया सह॥
translation: Where is that elder brother of Lakşmaņa of a mighty bow, furnished with teeth resembling Kunda flowers? If I live so long, I will behold him in company with Sītā.

sanskrit: लोहिताक्षं महाबाहुमामुक्तमणिकुण्डलम्। रामं यदि न पश्येयं गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्॥ अतो नु किं दुःखतरं योऽहमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम्। इमामवस्थामापनो नेह पश्यामि राघवम्॥
translation: What can be sadder than this, that reduced to such a pass, I cannot see here that descendant of Ikşvāku, Rāghava?

sanskrit: हा राम रामानुज हा हा वैदेहि तपस्विनि। न मां जानीत दुःखेन म्रियमाणमनाथवत्॥
translation: Ah Rāma! Ah you younger brother of Rāma! Ah you unfortunate Vaidehī! You do not know that I am through grief lamenting like one deserted.

sanskrit: स तेन राजा दुःखेन भृशमर्पितचेतनः। अवगाढः सुदुष्पारं शोकसागरमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Deprived of his consciousness through that sorrow of his, the king said.

sanskrit: रामशोकमहावेगः सीताविरहपारगः। श्वसितोर्मिमहावर्तो वाष्पवेगजलाविलः॥ बाहुविक्षेपमीनोऽसौ विक्रन्दितमहास्वनः। प्रकीर्णकेशशैवाल: कैकेयीवडवामुखः॥ ममाश्रुवेगप्रभवः कुब्जावाक्यमहाग्रहः। वरवेलो नृशंसाया रामप्रव्राजनायतः॥ यस्मिन् बत निमग्नोऽहं कौसल्ये राघवं विना। दुस्तरो जीवता देवि मयायं शोकसागरः॥ अशोभनं योऽहमिहाद्य राघवं दिदृक्षमाणो न लभे सलक्ष्मणम्। इतीव राजा विलपन् महायशाः पपात तूर्णं शयने स मूर्च्छितः॥
translation: I have plunged myself into this ocean of woe hard to cross, with grief for Rāma as its mighty tide; separation from Sītā, its other shore; sighs heaved, its furious billows and whirlpools; tears, rivers that rush into it; tossing of the arms, its fishes; lamentations it roar; my hair flung about, its moss; Kaikeyi, its submarine fire; my fastflowing tears, its current; the words of the humpbacked one, its terrific ravenous animals; the boon, its continents; and the exile of Rama, its expanse. And, O Kausalyā, without Rāghava, I shall sink in this ocean. O exalted dame, living, it is hard for me to cross over this ocean. It is surely owing to my sin that to-day wishing to behold Rāghava and Lakşmaņa, I do not get them (before me). Having thus lamented, the illustrious king all of a sudden dropped to the earth in a swoon.

sanskrit: इति विलपति पार्थिवे प्रणष्टे करुणतरं द्विगुणं च रामहेतोः। वचनमनुनिशम्य तस्य देवी भयमगमत् पुनरेव राममाता॥
translation: On the king swooning away lamenting, that exalted lady, Rāma's mother, hearing his words doubly bitter and more piteous than ever uttered for Rāma, was seized with fresh apprehension.

sanskrit: इति विलपति पार्थिवे प्रणष्टे करुणतरं द्विगुणं च रामहेतोः। वचनमनुनिशम्य तस्य देवी भयमगमत् पुनरेव राममाता॥
translation: On the king swooning away lamenting, that exalted lady, Rāma's mother, hearing his words doubly bitter and more piteous than ever uttered for Rāma, was seized with fresh apprehension.

sanskrit: ततो भूतोपसृष्टेव वेपमाना पुनः पुनः। धरण्यां गतसत्त्वेव कौसल्या सूतमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Then like one possessed by an evil spirit, and trembling again and again, Kausalyä lying down on the ground like one dead, spoke to the charioteer, saying.

sanskrit: नय मां यत्र काकुत्स्थ: सीता यत्र च लक्ष्मणः। तान् विना क्षणमप्यद्य जीवितुं नोत्सहे ह्यहम्॥
translation: Do you take me where Kākutstha is and Sītā and Lakşınaņa: without them, I cannot live for a moment.

sanskrit: निवर्तय रथं शीघ्रं दण्डकान् नय मामपि। अथ तान् नानुगच्छामि गमिष्यामि यमक्षयम्॥
translation: Do you without delay turn the car. Do you take me also to Dandaka. If I do not follow them, I shall repair to the mansion of Yama.

sanskrit: बाष्पवेगोपहतया स वाचा सज्जमानया। इदमासयन् देवीं सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्॥ त्यज शोकं च मोहं च सम्भ्रंमं दुःखजं तथा। व्यवधूय च संतापं वने वत्स्यति राघवः॥
translation: Thereat the cahrioteer with joined hands comforted that exalted lady with ready words faltering and choked with rising vapour, "Do you leave grief and sorrow and the violent emotion. Renouncing grief, Rāghava is living in the woods."

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणश्चापि रामस्य पादौ परिचरन् वने। आराधयति धर्मज्ञः परलोकं जितेन्द्रियः॥
translation: And in the forest, the righteous Laksmara, having his senses under control, is ministering to Răma's feet and is thus adoring the gods for happiness in the next world.

sanskrit: विजनेऽपि वने सीता वासं प्राप्य गृहेष्विव। विस्रम्भं लभतेऽभीता राम विन्यस्तमानसा॥
translation: And even in the lonely woods, Sītā as if remaining at home, having fixed her thoughts on Rāma, is living a life of love.

sanskrit: नास्या दैन्यं कृतं किंचित् सुसूक्ष्मपि लक्ष्यते। उचितेव प्रवासानां वैदेही प्रतिभाति मे॥
translation: And there appears not the least trace of any distress afflicting her; and Vaidehi seems to me as if she were meant (by Nature) for a life away from home.

sanskrit: नगरोपवनं गत्वा यथा स्म रमते पुरा। तथैव रमते सीता निर्जनेषु वनेष्वपि॥
translation: And as forinerly going to urban villas she disported, she disports now even in the lonely forest.

sanskrit: बालेव रमते सीताबालचन्द्रनिभानना। रामा रामे ह्यदीनात्मा विजनेऽपि वने सती॥
translation: And although living in the lone forest, that one of a countenance resembling the infant moon, sports merrily like a girl, in the garden represented by Rāma's self.

sanskrit: तद्गतं हृदयं यस्यास्तदधीनं च जीवितम्। अयोध्या हि भवेदस्या रामहीना तथा वनम्॥
translation: Ayodhyā without Rāma would have seemed a wilderness to her whose heart is fixed on him and whose very life depends upon him.

sanskrit: परिपृच्छति वैदेही ग्रामांश्च नगराणि च। गतिं दृष्ट्वा नदीनां च पादपान् विविधानपि॥ रामं वा लक्ष्मणं वापि दृष्ट्वा जानाति जानकी। अयोध्या क्रोशमात्रे तु विहारमिव साश्रिता।१३।।
translation: Vaidehī is now asking (Rāma) concerning the villages and towns (in their way); and observing various trees and the courses of the rivers, Jānaki, asking Råma Laksmana (for information), is learning all about them. And Sītā sports as she used to do in arbours stationed at the distance of only one krosa from Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: इदमेव स्मराम्यस्याः सहसैवोपजल्पितम्। कैकेयीसंश्रितं जल्पं नेदानी प्रतिभाति माम्॥
translation: This only I remember; but all that she had from sudden impulse communicated to me or concerning Kaikeyſ, does not rise into consciousness.

sanskrit: ध्वंसयित्वा तु तद् वाक्यं प्रमादात् पर्युपस्थितम्। ह्लादनं वचनं सूतो देव्या मधुरमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Suppressing this topic which had come up through heedlessness, the charioteer spoke sweet words cheering up that noble lady.

sanskrit: अध्वना वातवेगेन सम्भ्रमेणातपेन च। न विगच्छति वैदेह्याश्चन्द्रांशुसदृशी प्रभा॥
translation: Neither through the fatigue of travel, nor the influence of the wind, nor excitement, nor the sun, has Vaidehi's lustre resembling the lunar light suffered any diminution.

sanskrit: सदृशं शतपत्रस्य पूर्णचन्द्रोपमप्रभम्। वदनं तद् वदान्याया. वैदेह्या न विकम्पते ॥
translation: The countenance of that fair-speaking one resembling the lotus and comparable to the full moon in splendour, has not waxed pale.

sanskrit: अलक्तरसरक्ताभावलक्तरसवर्जितौ। अद्यापि चरणौ तस्याः पद्मकोशसमप्रभौ॥
translation: Her feet now without your dye of the liquid lac, but naturally furnished with the roseate hue of the same, are gorgeous like lotus buds.

sanskrit: नूपुरोत्कृष्टलीलेव खेलं गच्छति भामिनी। इदानीमपि वैदेही तद्रागान्यस्तभूषणा ॥
translation: Still Vaidehī decked in ornaments from affection for Rāma, goes gracefully rebuking with her bangles the wavy gait (of cranes).

sanskrit: गजं वा वीक्ष्य सिंह वा व्याघ्र वा वनमाश्रिता। नाहारयति संत्रासं बाहू रामस्य संश्रिता॥
translation: Supporting herself on Rāma's arm, Sītă arrived at the forest, is not inspired with fear on beholding either an elephant, or a lion, or a tiger.

sanskrit: न शोच्यस्ते न चात्मा ते शोच्यो नापि जनाधिपः। इदं हि चरितं लोके प्रतिष्ठास्यति शाश्वतम्॥
translation: Therefore they are not to be bewailed, nor your own self, nor the lord of men. This history of Rāma will endure for ever in this world.

sanskrit: विधूय शोकं परिहृष्टमानसा महर्षियाते पथि सुव्यवस्थिताः। वने रता वन्यफलाशनाः पितुः शुभां प्रतिज्ञा प्रतिपालयन्ति ते॥
translation: Renouncing grief and with cheerful hearts, well established in the life led by the Maharşis, they living in the forest on wild fruits as their sustenance, are maintaining the noble promise of their sire.

sanskrit: तथापि सूतेन सुयुक्तवादिना निवार्यमाणा सुतशोककर्शिता। न चैव देवी विरराम कूजितात् प्रियेति पुत्रेति च राघवेति च ॥
translation: Consoled by the truth-telling yet sweetspeeched charioteer, that lady oppressed with grief for her son, ceased not to wail loudly, "My beloved,” “My son," "Rāghava."

sanskrit: वनं गते धर्मरते रामे रमयतां वरे। कौसल्या रुदती चार्ता भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्॥
translation: On that foremost of those capable of charming people, the righteous Rāma, repairing to the forest, Kausalyā crying in grief said to her husband.

sanskrit: यद्यपि त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रथितं ते महद् यशः। सानुक्रोशो वदान्यश्च प्रियवादी च राघवः॥
translation: Your great fame has spread over the three worlds; and the descendant of Raghu is kind, munificent and fair-speaking.

sanskrit: कथं नरवर श्रेष्ठ पुत्रौ तौ सह सीतया। दुःखितौ सुखसंवृद्धौ वने दुःखं सहिष्यतः॥
translation: Why then have you forsaken those foremost of men along with Sītā? Brought up in happiness, and now brought to misery, how can they bear it?

sanskrit: सा नूनं तरुणी श्यामा सुकुमारी सुखोचिता। कथमुष्णं च शीतं च मैथिली विसहिष्यते॥
translation: How can the youthful daughter of Mithilā of slender make, tender, and deserving of happiness, bear heat and cold?

sanskrit: भुक्त्वाशनं विशालाक्षी सूपदंशान्वितं शुभम्। वन्यं नैवारमाहारं कथं सीतोपभोक्ष्यते॥
translation: Having formerly partaken of (excellent) rice with curries, how will Sita feed on wild rice?

sanskrit: गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा शुभसमन्विता। कथं क्रव्यादसिंहानां शब्दं श्रोष्यत्यशोभनम्॥
translation: Having heard excellent vocal and instrumental music, how will Sītă hear the frightful cries of carnivorous lions?

sanskrit: महेन्द्रध्वजसंकाशः क्व नु शेते महाभुजः। भुजं परिघसंकाशमुपाधाय महाबलः॥
translation: Resembling the gonfalon of the great Indra, where sleeps the mighty-armed and exceedingly powerful Råma, making his arm like to a mace his pillow?

sanskrit: पद्मवर्णं सुकेशान्तं पद्मनिःश्वासमुत्तमम्। कदा द्रक्ष्यामि रामस्य वदनं पुष्करेक्षणम्॥
translation: When shall I behold Rāma's countenance hued like the lotus, with his hair ending beautifully (in curls), and his breath impregnated with the fine perfume of the lotus, and his eyes resembling lotus leaves?

sanskrit: वज्रसारमयं नूनं हृदयं मे न संशयः। अपश्यन्त्या न तं यद् वै फलतीदं सहस्रधा॥
translation: Surely my heart, without doubt, is made of the essence of the thunderbolt, since not beholding him, it is not cracked in a thousand fragments.

sanskrit: यत् त्वया करुणं कर्म व्यपोह्य मम बान्धवाः। निरस्ताः परिधावन्ति सुखार्हाः कृपणा वने॥
translation: It is because of your sad act that mine own, being thwarted, although worthy of happiness, are miserably ranging the wilderness.

sanskrit: यदि पञ्चदशे वर्षे राघवः पुनरेष्यति। जह्याद् राज्यं च कोशं च भरतो नोपलक्ष्यते॥
translation: If after the expiration of the five and ten years, Rāghava does return, it does not appear likely that Bharata will renounce the kingdom and the exchequer.

sanskrit: भोजयन्ति किल श्राद्धे केचित् स्वानेव बान्धवान्। ततः पश्चात् समीक्षन्ते कृतकार्या द्विजोत्तमान्॥ तत्र ये गुणवन्तश्च विद्वांसश्च द्विजातयः। न पश्चात् तेऽभिमन्यन्ते सुधामपि सुरोपमाः॥
translation: Some on the occasions of the Sradha (first) feast their own friends, and having done this, they mind the choice Brāhmaṇas. But those twice-born ones that are meritorious, learned, and like to celestials, do not at the last moment regard even viands resembling ambrosia.

sanskrit: ब्राह्मणेष्वपि वृत्तेषु भुक्तशेष द्विजोत्तमाः। नाभ्युपेतुमलं प्राज्ञाः शृङ्गच्छेदमिवर्षभाः॥
translation: Brāhmaṇas of high respectability endowed with wisdom never bear being entertained after the other twice-born ones have been feasted, even as bulls never quietly bear to have their horns cut off.

sanskrit: एवं कनीयसा भ्रात्रा भुक्तं राज्यं विशाम्पते। भ्राता ज्येष्ठो वरिष्ठश्च किमर्थं नावमन्यते॥
translation: Why will not an elder brother and one who has sterling merits, O monarch, disregard a kingdom which has been thus enjoyed by his younger brother?

sanskrit: न परेणाहृतं भक्ष्यं व्याघ्रः खादितुमिच्छति। एवमेव नरव्याघ्रः परलीढं न मंस्यते॥
translation: A tiger does not like to feed on food procured by others. Even so that tiger-like personage does not regard anything that has come to be tasted by another.

sanskrit: हविराज्यं पुरोडाशः कुशा यूपाश्च खादिराः। नैतानि यातयामानि कुर्वन्ति पुनरध्वरे ॥
translation: Clarified butter, sacrificial cakes, Kusa, stakes of catechu having been used in one sacrifice cannot be used in another.

sanskrit: तथा ह्यात्तमिदं राज्यं हृतसारां सुरामिव। नाभिमन्तुमलं रामो नष्टसोममिवाध्वरम्॥
translation: Even so this kingdom which has been already enjoyed, like to liquor deprived of its essence or a sacrifice whose soma has been eaten, cannot be accepted by Rāma.

sanskrit: नैवंविधमसत्कारं राघवो मर्षयिष्यति। बलवानिव शार्दूलो वालधेरभिमर्शनम्॥
translation: Such an ill treatment Rāghava will not put up with, even as a powerful tiger cannot bear the rubbing of its tail (by another).

sanskrit: नैतस्य सहिता लोका भयं कुर्युर्महामृधे। अधर्मं त्विह धर्मात्मा लोकं धर्मेण योजयेत्॥
translation: This world aided by the gods fear to encounter him in high conflict; but he restrains himself, thinking any such action on his part as unrighteous. Indeed, that righteous one brings back people to morality.

sanskrit: नन्वसौ काञ्चनैर्बाणैर्महावीर्यो महाभुजः। युगान्त इव भूतानि सागरानपि निर्दहेत्॥
translation: Surely, that mighty-armed one endowed with exceeding prowess, can with his golden shafts burn all creatures and the oceans, like the Day at the dissolution of all.

sanskrit: स तादृशः सिंहबलो वृषभाक्षो नरर्षभः। स्वयमेव हतः पित्रा जलजेनात्मजो यथा॥
translation: But such a man of men, possessed of leonine strength, and graced with the eyes of a bull, has been destroyed by his father, like a fish destroying his offspring.

sanskrit: द्विजातिचरितो धर्मः शास्त्रे दृष्टः सनातनैः। यदि ते धर्मनिरते त्वया पुत्रे विवासिते॥
translation: If you had believed in the morality prescribed in the scriptures, and which is followed by the twice-born ones, you would not have banished your son. But disregarding such morality, you have banished your virtuous son.

sanskrit: गतिरेका पतिर्नार्या द्वितीया गतिरात्मजः। तृतीया ज्ञातयो राजश्चतुर्थी नैव विद्यते॥
translation: One of the refuges of a woman is her husband, a second is her son, and a third is her relatives; and a fourth she has none.

sanskrit: तत्र त्वं मम नैवासि रामश्च वनमाहितः। न वनं गन्तुमिच्छामि सर्वथा हा हता त्वया॥
translation: But you cease to be mine; and Rāma has been sent to the woods. I do not like to go into the forest; so I am entirely undone by you.

sanskrit: हतं त्वया राष्ट्रमिदं सराज्यं हताः स्म सर्वाः सह मन्त्रिभिश्च। हता सपुत्रास्मि हताश्चं पौराः सुतश्च भार्या च तव प्रहृष्टौ ॥
translation: This kingdom, your own kingdom, has been destroyed by you; destroyed are all along with the counsellors; destroyed am I with my son; and destroyed are the citizens: your son and your wife are alone delighted.

sanskrit: इमां गिरं दारुणशब्दसंहितां निशम्य रामेति मुमोह दुःखितः। ततः स शोकं प्रविवेश पार्थिवः स्वदुष्कृतं चापि पुनस्तथास्मरत्॥
translation: Hearing these words uttered in heart-rending accents, Dasaratha exceedingly distressed, became senseless. And being afflicted with grief, he again remembered his evil act.

sanskrit: एवं तु क्रुद्धया राजा राममात्रा सशोकया। श्रावितः परुषं वाक्यं चिन्तयामास दुःखितः॥ चिन्तयित्वा स च नृपो मोहव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः। अथ दीर्पण कालेन संज्ञामाप परंतपः॥
translation: Thus harshly addressed by the indignant mother of Rāma, the king aggrieved was plunged in thought. Having thought for a long while, that repressor of foes, the king, who had lost his senses through grief, regained consciousness.

sanskrit: स संज्ञामुपलभ्यैव दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वसन्। कौसल्या पार्श्वतो दृष्ट्वा ततश्चिन्तामुपागमत्॥
translation: Having regained his senses, he sighing hot and hard, seeing Kausalyā beside him, was again lost in thought.

sanskrit: तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य प्रत्यभात् कर्म दुष्कृतम्। यदनेन कृतं पूर्वमज्ञानाच्छब्दवेधिना॥
translation: As he was thinking, the sinful act which he had through ignorance formerly committed by means of the shaft which hits by sounds, rose up in his recollection,

sanskrit: अमानास्तेन शोकेन रामशोकेन च प्रभुः। द्वाभ्यामपि महाराजः शोकाभ्यामभितप्यते॥
translation: Afflicted with this grief as well as that on account of Rāma, that lord, the king, burned in these two several griefs.

sanskrit: दह्यमानस्तु शोकाभ्यां कौसल्यामाह दुःखितः। वेपमानोऽञ्जलिं कृत्वा प्रसादार्थमवाङ्मुखः। ॥
translation: Burning in grief and distressed, he trembling and with joined hands, with his head hanging down, addressed Kausalyā, with the view of pacifying her.

sanskrit: प्रसादये त्वां कौसल्ये रचितोऽयं मयाञ्जलिः। वत्सला चानृशंसा च त्वं हि नित्यं परेष्वपि॥
translation: I deprecate your displeasure. O Kausalyä with joined hands. You are ever affectionate and did not treat harshly even enemies.

sanskrit: कौसल्या व्यसृजद् भर्ता तु खलु नारीणां गुणवान् निर्गुणोऽपि वा। धर्मं विमृशमानानां प्रत्यक्षं देवि दैवतम्॥
translation: Verily to women cognizant of virtue, a husband, whether he has any merits or not, is a very deity.

sanskrit: सा त्वं धर्मपरा नित्यं दृष्टलोकपरावरा। नार्हसे विप्रियं वक्तुं दुःखितापि सुदुःखितम्॥
translation: Ever virtuous, you, that have seen both the virtuous and the vicious, although aggrieved, ought not to say anything unpleasant to me who am weighed down with woe.

sanskrit: तद् वाक्यं करुणं राज्ञः श्रुत्वा दीनस्य भाषितम्। बाष्पं प्रणालीव नवोदकम्॥
translation: Having heard these piteous words of the distressed king, Kausalyā uttered words even as a water-way lets out fresh accession of rain.

sanskrit: सा मूर्ध्नि बद्ध्वा रुदती राज्ञः पद्ममिवाञ्जलिम्। सम्भ्रमादब्रवीत् त्रस्ता त्वरमाणाक्षरं वचः॥
translation: And weeping, she drew on her head the joined hands of the king resembling lotuses; and then flurried spoke these words hurriedly informed with extreme affection.

sanskrit: प्रसीद शिरसा याचे भूमौ निपतितास्मि ते। याचितास्मि हता देव क्षन्तव्याहं नहि त्वया॥
translation: Be you propitious; I beseech with (bended) head. I bow to you, falling on the ground. O reverend one, besought by you, I shall be undone. I do not deserve to be forgiven by you.

sanskrit: नैषा हि सा स्त्री भवति श्लाघनीयेन धीमता। उभयोर्लोकयोर्लोके पत्या या सम्प्रसाद्यते॥
translation: She cannot be reckoned a gentlewoman, who is propitiated by her intelligent husband, worthy of being extolled in both worlds.

sanskrit: जानामि धर्मे धर्मज्ञ त्वां जाने सत्यवादिनम्। पुत्रशोकार्तया तत्तु मया किमपि भाषितम्॥
translation: I know duty, O righteous one; I know that you are truth-telling. And it is because I was exceedingly distressed on account of my son that I spoke harshly to you.

sanskrit: शोको नाशयते धैर्यं शोको नाशयते श्रुतम्। शोको नाशयते सर्वं नास्ति शोकसमो रिपुः॥
translation: Sorrow destroys patience, sorrow destroys knowledge of the scriptures, sorrow destroys every things; there is no enemy like to sorrow.

sanskrit: शक्यमापतितः सोढुं प्रहारो रिपुहस्ततः। शोढुमापतितः शोकः सुसूक्ष्मोऽपि न शक्यते॥
translation: One can falling down bear ever beating from an enemy; but one cannot falling down bear ever so little sorrow.

sanskrit: वनवासाय रामस्य पञ्चरात्रोऽत्र गण्यते। यः शोकहतहर्षायाः पञ्चवर्षोपमो मम॥
translation: This is the fifth night of the banishment of Rāma, as calculated by me; and to me rendered cheerless by sorrow, this interval has assumed the proportions of five years.

sanskrit: तं हि चिन्तयमानायाः शोकोऽयं हृदि वर्धते। नदीनामिव वेगेन समुद्रसलिलं महत्॥
translation: And fostered by thought on my part, this grief increases in my bosom, like the mighty waters of the ocean increased by the vehement discharge of rivers.

sanskrit: एवं हि कथयन्त्यास्तु कौसल्यायाः शुभं वचः। मन्दरश्मिरभूत् सूर्यो रजनी चाभ्यवर्तत॥ अथ प्रह्लादितो वाक्यैर्देव्या कौसल्यया नृपः। शोकेन चसमाक्रान्तो निद्राया वशमेयिवान्॥
translation: As Kausalyā was thus speaking auspiciously, the rays of the sun grew milder, and the night arrived. Cheered up by the words of Kausalya, the king overcome by grief, felt the influence of sleep.

sanskrit: प्रतिबुद्धो मुहूर्तेन शोकोपहतचेतनः। अथ राजा दशरथः स चिन्तामभ्यपद्यत ॥
translation: Starting in a moment from sleep, king Dasaratha deprived (almost) of his consciousness by grief, (again) became a prey to thought.

sanskrit: रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चैव विवासाद् वासवोपमम्। आपेदे उपसर्गस्तं तमः सूर्यमिवासुरम्॥
translation: I consequence of the exile of Rāma and Laks mana, the king resembling Våsava was overpowered by grief, like the darkness of Rāhu enveloping the sun. was own

sanskrit: सभार्ये हि गते रामे कौसल्यां कोसलेश्वरः। विवक्षुरसितापाङ्गी स्मृत्वा दुष्कृतमात्मनः॥
translation: Then on Răma's having gone along with his wife, the lord of the Kosalas, remembering his own misdeed, felt anxious to communicate himself to that lady having her eyes furnished with dark outer corners.

sanskrit: स राजा रजनी षष्ठी रामे प्रवाजिते वनम्। अर्धरात्रे दशरथः सोऽस्मरद् दुष्कृतं कृतम्॥
translation: And on the sixth night after Rāma had repaired to the forest, the king Dasaratha, when it midnight, remembered his unrighteous act.

sanskrit: स राजा पुत्रशोकार्तः स्मृत्वा दुष्कृतमात्मनः। कौसल्यां पुत्रशोकार्तामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
translation: And then to Kausalyā aggrieved on account of her son, her spoke these words.

sanskrit: यदाचरति कल्याणि शुभं वा यदि वाऽशुभम्। तदेव लभते भद्रे कर्ता कर्मजमात्मनः॥
translation: As are the actions of one, O auspicious one, whether good otherwise, the consequences, O gentle lady, reaped by the doer of them.

sanskrit: गुरुलाघवमर्थानामारम्भे कर्मणां फलम्। दोषं वा यो न जानाति स बाल इति होच्यते।७।।
translation: He that on the eve of beginning an action either relating to this world or the next, does not take into consideration the fact that actions entail consequences light or grave, disagreeable (or otherwise), is styled a child.

sanskrit: कश्चिदाम्रवणं छित्त्वा पलाशांश्च निषिञ्चति। पुष्पं दृष्ट्वा फले गृध्नुः स शोचति फलागमे॥ अविज्ञाय फलं यो हि कर्म त्वेवानुधावति। स शोचेत् फलवेलायां यथा किंशुकसेचकः॥
translation: He that cutting down a mango grove, waters Palasa trees, beholding the flowers (blooming), will covet fruits; and grieve when their season arrives. The person that without apprehending (the principle of causation) rushed to action, grieves at the season of fruits, even like him that waters kinsuka trees (hewing down his mango grove). or are

sanskrit: सोऽहमाम्रवणं छित्वा पलाशांश्च न्यषेचयम्। राम फलागमे त्यक्त्वा पश्चाच्छोचामि दुर्मतिः॥
translation: And is this way, I fool that I am having hewn down my grove of mangoes and watered Palāsas, having renounced Räma in the season of fruit, is grieving in the end.

sanskrit: लब्धशब्देन कौसल्ये कुमारेण धनुष्मता। कुमारः शब्दवेधीति मया पापमिदं कृतम्॥
translation: Having, O Kausalyā, earned the expression, 'The Prince can pierce his aim by sound alone,', I, a prince and bowman, did this offence.

sanskrit: तदिदं मेऽनुसम्प्राप्तं देवि दुःखं स्वयंकृतम्। सम्मोहादिह बालेन यथा स्याद् भक्षितं विषम्॥
translation: Therefore, O noble dame, I have myself brought this misfortune on me, like a child who has eaten poison through ignorance.

sanskrit: यथान्यः पुरुषः कश्चित् पलाशैर्मोहितो भवेत्। एवं मयाप्यविज्ञातं शब्दवेध्यमिदं फलम्॥
translation: Even like another person fascinated by the sight of some Palasa trees (and doing as mentioned above), I (did this act) not fore knowing the consequence that would follow my shooting by sound.

sanskrit: देव्यनूढा त्वमभवो युवराजो भवाम्यहम्। ततः प्रावृडनुप्राप्ता मम कामविवर्धिनी॥
translation: O lady, you were then unwedded; and I was a youthful prince. And it was at this time that the rainy season increasing my desire set in.

sanskrit: अपास्य हि रसान् भौमांस्तप्त्वा च जगदंशुभिः। परेताचरितां भीमां रविराचरते दिशम् ॥
translation: Drawing moisture from the ground and heated the earth by his rays, the Sun goes to the dreadful quarter whither repair the dead.

sanskrit: उष्णमन्तर्दधे सद्यः स्निग्धा ददृशिरे घनाः। ततो जहषिरे सर्वे भेकसारङ्गबर्हिणः॥ क्लिनपक्षोत्तराः स्नाताः कृच्छ्रादिव पतत्रिणः। वृष्टिवातावधूताग्रान् पादपानभिपेदिरे॥
translation: The heat was immediately dispelled, and the gelid clouds snowed themselves; and frogs and Sārangas and peacocks began to rejoice; and, finding it unpleasant, the feathered ones bathed and with the surface of their plumage shrunk up from the wet, took refuge in trees shaken by the wind and rain.

sanskrit: पतितेनाम्भसाऽऽच्छन्नः पतमानेन चासकृत्। आबभौ मत्तसारङ्गस्तोयराशिरिवाचलः॥
translation: And the hill graced by maddened Sārangas, covered by showers falling simultaneously looked like a mass of waters.

sanskrit: पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि स्रोतांसि विमलान्यपि। सुस्रुवुर्गिरिधातुभ्यः सभस्मानि भुजंगवत्॥
translation: And the waters although unstained, being mixed up with mineral substances and ashes from the mountains, flowed in serpentine torrents black and red.

sanskrit: तस्मिन्नतिसुखे काले धनुष्मानिषुमान् रथी। व्यायामकृतसंकल्पः सरयूमन्वगां नदीम्॥ निपाने महिषं रात्रौ गजं वाभ्यागतं मृगम्। अन्यद्वाश्वापदं किंचिज्जिघांसुरजितेन्द्रियः॥
translation: At such a sweet hour, I intent upon taking exercise, taking my bow and arrows and mounted on my car, sallied out for the river Sarayū, with the intention that I with my senses under control, should in the watery expense slay any buffalo, elephant, or any other beast that mighty have come there in the night.

sanskrit: अथान्धकारे त्वौषं जले कुम्भस्य पूर्यतः। अचक्षुर्विषये घोषं वारणस्येव नर्दतः॥
translation: And (coming there) while it was so dark that : nothing could be discovered, I heard sounds of a filling pitcher proceeding from the waters; resembling the roars of an elephant.

sanskrit: ततोऽहं शरमुद्धृत्य दीप्तमाशीविषोपमम्। शब्दं प्रति गजप्रेप्सुरभिलक्ष्यमपातयम्॥
translation: Thereupon raising up my shaft flaming and like to a serpent of virulent poison, I desirous of hunting the (imaginary) elephant, let fly my shaft in the direction of the sound.

sanskrit: अमुञ्चं निशितं बाणमहमाशीविषोपमम्। तत्र वागुषसि व्यक्ता प्रादुरासीद् वनौकसः॥ हा हेति पततस्तोये बाणाद् व्यथितमर्मणः। तस्मिन्निपतिते भूमौ वागभूत् तत्र मानुषी॥
translation: Thereupon from the spot whereto the sharpened shaft resembling a poisonous snake had been discharged by me in the twilight, proceeded cries of 'Oh' and 'Alas' uttered by a forester pierced to the quick by the arrow, and falling into the water. And when he had dropped down, words spoken by a human being became audible.

sanskrit: कथमस्मद्विधे शस्त्रं निपतेच्च तपस्विनी। प्रविविक्तां नदी रात्रावुदाहारोऽहमागतः॥
translation: Why does the weapon light upon me? I had come to this lone stream for procuring water.

sanskrit: इषुणाभिहतः केन कस्य वापकृतं मया। ऋषेहि न्यस्तदण्डस्य वने वन्येन जीवतः॥ कथं नु शस्त्रेण वधो मद्विधस्य विधीयते। जटाभारधरस्यैव वल्कलाजिनवाससः॥ को वधेन ममार्थी स्यात् किं वास्यापकृतं मया। एवं निष्फलमारब्धं केवलानर्थसंहितम्॥
translation: By whom have I been wounded by this arrow? To whom have I done wrong? And how can the slaying of one like me bearing a load of matted locks, and wearing bark and deer-skin, who subsist on what the forest yields and never injures others, be sanctioned by the scriptures? Who can serve any purpose by slaying me? And how can I have injured such an one? Such a purposeless act cannot but end in evil.

sanskrit: न क्वचित् साधु मन्येत नेमं तथानुशोचामि जीवितक्षयमात्मनः॥ मातरं पितरं चोभावनुशोचामि मद्वधे। तदेतन्मिथुनं वृद्धं चिरकालभृतं मया॥ मयि पञ्चत्वमापन्ने कां वृत्तिं वर्तयिष्यति। वृद्धौ च मातापितरावहं चैकेषुणा हतः॥ केन स्म निहताः सर्वे सुबालेनाकृतात्मना।
translation: This can never be reckoned as righteous even like to violating the chastity of a preceptor's wife. I do not so much lament my end as I lament it on account of my father and mother. To what will the old couple, who have ever been maintained by me, betake themselves when I am gone? My father and mother are old, and I their only son is slain. What boy is it of uncontrolled senses that has killed us all?

sanskrit: यथैव गुरुतल्पगम्। तां गिरं करुणं श्रुत्वा मम धर्मानुकाक्षिणः॥ कराभ्यां सशरं चापं व्यथितस्यापतद् भुवि। तस्याहं करुणं श्रुत्वा ऋषेर्विलपतो निशि॥ सम्भ्रान्तः शोकवेगेन भृशमासं विचेतनः।
translation: Hearing his piteous words, I ever anxious to follow virtue, was exceedingly pained, and the bow with its arrow fixed fell down from my hand to the earth.

sanskrit: तं देशमहमागम्य दीनसत्त्वः सुदुर्मनाः॥ अपश्यमिषुणा तीरे सरय्वास्तापसं हतम्। अवकीर्णजटाभारं प्रविद्धकलशोदकम्॥ पांसुशोणितदिग्धाङ्ग शयानं शल्यवेधितम्। स मामुद्वीक्ष्य नेत्राभ्यां त्रस्तमस्वस्थचेतनम्॥ इत्युवाच वचः क्रूरं दिधक्षनिव तेजसा।
translation: Hearing in the night, the pathetic words of the saint thus lamenting, I became frightened, and was deprived of my senses through excess of grief. And coming to the quarter, I exceedingly unnerved and with an excited mind, discovered on the banks of the Sarayū an ascetic wounded with a shaft, with his matted locks scattered about, his pitcher of water lying by, his body smeared with blood and dust and afflicted by the dare. Gazing with his eyes at me who was extremely agitated and ill at ease, he said these words sternly, as if consuming me with his energy.

sanskrit: किं तवापकृतं राजन् वने निवसता मया॥ जिहीर्घरम्भो गुर्वर्थं यदहं ताडितस्त्वया।
translation: What wrong, O monarch, had I residing in the woods done you, that coming to procure water for my parents, I have been thus afflicted by. you?

sanskrit: बाणेन मर्मण्यभिहते मयि ॥ द्वावन्धौ निहतौ वृद्धौ माता जनयिता च मे।
translation: By piercing my marrow with a shaft, you have slain both my aged and blind father and mother.

sanskrit: तौ नूनं दुर्बलावन्धौ मत्प्रतीक्षौ पिपासितौ॥ चिरमाशां कृतां कष्टां तृष्णां संधारयिष्यतः।
translation: Surely, they feeble and blind, who afflicted by thirst are remaining in expectation of me, will now bear (the stress and tension of) the expectation as well as the parching thirst.

sanskrit: एकेन खलु न नूनं तपसो वास्ति फलयोगः श्रुतस्य वा॥ पिता यन्मां न जानीते शयानं पतितं भुवि।
translation: Surely asceticism and study carry no fruit with them, since I lying low on the ground, my father knows nothing about it.

sanskrit: जानन्नपि च किं कुर्यादशक्तश्चापरिक्रमः।॥ भिद्यमानमिवाशक्तस्त्रातुमन्यो नगो नगम्।
translation: And what could he do, even if he knew it, being as he is incapable and unable to go about? One tree cannot rescue another that is being battered (by the winds).

sanskrit: पितुस्त्वमेव मे गत्वा शीघ्रमाचक्ष्व राघव॥ न त्वामनुदहेत् क्रुद्धो वनमग्निरिवैधितः।
translation: Do you, O descendant of Raghu, yourself going to my father, speedily inform of him this that has occurred. But take care that like a fire waxing furious consuming a woods, he in his ire do not burn you.

sanskrit: इयमेकपदी राजन् यतो मे पितुराश्रमः॥ तं प्रसादय गत्वा त्वं न त्वा संकुपितः शपेत्।
translation: This narrow way, O king, will lead you to my father's dwelling. Do you going there, pacify him, so that getting wroth he may not curse you.

sanskrit: विशल्यं कुरु मां राजन् मर्म मे निशितः शरः॥ रुणद्धि मृदु सोत्सेधं तीरमम्बुरयो यथा।
translation: Do you (now), O king, take out the arrow. Your sharpened shaft afflicts my marrow, like the tide of a river wearing away a hollowheaving sand bank.

sanskrit: सशल्यः क्लिश्यते प्राणैर्विशल्यो विनशिष्यति।४६।। इति मामविशच्चिन्ता तस्य शल्यापकर्षणे। दुःखितस्य च दीनस्य मम शोकातुरस्य च॥ लक्षयामास स ऋषिश्चिन्तां मुनिसुतस्तदा।
translation: But touching the extracting of the arrow, this thought perplexed me: 'If the arrow is left alone, it pains; if extracted, death ensues.' As I was distressed, aggrieved an afflicted with sorrow, the son of the ascetic perceived my anxiety.

sanskrit: ताम्यमानं स मां कृच्छादुवाच परमार्थवित्॥ सीदमानो विवृत्ताङ्गोऽचेष्टमानो गतः क्षयम्। संस्तभ्य शोकं धैर्येण स्थिरचित्तो भवाम्यहम्॥ ब्रह्महत्याकृतं तापं हृदयादपनीयताम्। न द्विजातिरहं राजन्मा भूत् ते मनसो व्यथा॥
translation: Thereupon that one well versed in the scriptures sinking motionless, with his eyes rolling upwards, and waxing extremely weak, said with difficulty, 'Restraining sorrow, I by dint of patience become calm. Do you remove from your mind the grief caused by the consciousness of having slain a Brāhmaṇa. O king, I belong not to the twice-born race: let not your mind be pained.

sanskrit: शूद्रायामस्मि वैश्येन जातो नरवराधिप। इतीव वदतः कृच्छाद् बाणाभिहतमर्मणः॥ विघूर्णतो विचेष्टस्य वेपमानस्य भूतले। तस्य त्वाताम्यमानस्य तं बाणमहमुद्धरम्। स मामुद्वीक्ष्य संत्रस्तो जहौ प्राणांस्तपोधनः॥
translation: O lord of the foremost men, I was begot by a Vaisya on a Sudra woman.' As he, his vitals afflicted with the shaft, hi eyes rolling, inert and trembling on the ground, with his limbs drawn in, was speaking with difficulty, I drew out the arrow. Thereupon, looking at me, the ascetic, growing affrighted, gave up the ghost.

sanskrit: जलाड़गात्रं तु विलप्य कृच्छं मर्मवणं संततमुच्छसन्तम्। ततः सरय्वां तमहं शयानं समीक्ष्य भद्रे सुभृशं विषण्णः॥
translation: On beholding him with his body dripping with water, and mortally wounded, and breathing hard without respite, after he had bewailed his mortal wound, lying on the banks of the Sarayü, I lamented him and was, O gentle lady, greatly aggrieved.

sanskrit: वधमप्रतिरूपं तु महर्षेस्तस्य राघवः। विलपन्नेव धर्मात्मा कौसल्यामिदमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Remembering the extraordinary death of the Maharsi, that righteous descendant of Raghu, lamenting his son, thus spoke to Kausalyā.

sanskrit: तदज्ञानान्महत्पापं कृत्वा संकुलितेन्द्रियः। एकस्त्वचिन्तयं बुद्ध्या कथं नु सुकृतं भवेत्॥
translation: Having unwittingly committed that great sin, I, with my senses oppressed through grief, thought within myself as to how I could mend it.

sanskrit: ततस्तं घटमादाय पूर्णं परमवारिणा। आश्रमं तमहं प्राप्य यथाख्यातपथं गतः॥
translation: Then taking up the pitcher filled with excellent water, I went by the way mentioned and (at last) reached the asylum.

sanskrit: तत्राहं दुर्बलावन्धौ वृद्धावपरिणायकौ। अपश्यं तस्य पितरौ लूनपक्षाविव द्विजौ॥ तन्निमित्ताभिरासीनौ कथाभिरपरिश्रमौ। तामाशां मत्कृते हीनावुपासीनावनाथवत्॥
translation: There I found his aged, infirm, forlorn, parents, without any one to help them in moving about, like to birds whose wings have been severed, keeping up a talk about (their son) without experiencing any fatigue, and like helpless ones feeding on a hope which had been blasted by me.

sanskrit: शोकोपहतचित्तश्च भयसंत्रस्तचेतनः। तच्चाश्रमपदं गत्वा भूयः शोकमहं गतः॥
translation: My senses overpowered by grief, and my consciousness almost lost through apprehension, I, arrived at the hermitage, again overwhelmed with sorrow.

sanskrit: पदशब्दं तु मे श्रुत्वा मुनिर्वाक्यमभाषत। किं चिरायसि मे पुत्र पानीयं क्षिप्रमानय॥
translation: Hearing my footsteps, the ascetic said, “Why, my son, delay you? Bring the drink at once.

sanskrit: यनिमित्तमिदं तात सलिले क्रीडितं त्वया। उत्कण्ठिता ते मातेयं प्रविश क्षिप्रमाश्रमम्॥
translation: Your mother, O child, was exceedingly anxious in consequence of your sporting in the waters. Do you speedily enter the asylum.

sanskrit: यद् व्यलीकं कृतं पुत्र मात्रा ते यदि वा मया। न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं त्वया तात तपस्विना॥
translation: O child, it behove you not to take to heart any unkind action that, O son, may have been done to you of high fame either by your mother or myself.

sanskrit: त्वं गतिस्त्वगतीनां च चक्षुस्त्वं हीनचक्षुषाम्। समासक्तास्त्वयि प्राणाः कथं त्वं नाभिभाषसे॥
translation: You are the resource of these helpless ones; you are the eyes of these bereft of their sight. was Our lives are bound up with you. Why do not answer?'

sanskrit: मुनिमव्यक्तया वाचा तमहं सज्जमानया। हीनव्यञ्जनया प्रेक्ष्य भीतचित्त इवाब्रुवम्॥ मनसः कर्म चेष्टाभिरभिसंस्तभ्य वाग्बलम्। आचचक्षे त्वंहं तस्मै पुत्रव्यसनजं भयम्॥
translation: Seeing the ascetic with a choked utterance indistinctly speaking thus with the letters not articulated clearly, I, dashed in spirits, yet concealing the real state of my mind by assuming a doughty tongue, communicated to him the danger that had befallen him in consequence of the calamity of his son:

sanskrit: क्षत्रियोऽहं दशरथो नाहं पुत्रो महात्मनः। सज्जनावमतं दुःखमिदं प्राप्तं स्वकर्मजम् ॥
translation: I am a Ksatriya, Dasaratha (by name), and no son of yours, O magnanimous one. I have come by a misfortune in consequence of an act blamed by the good.

sanskrit: भगवंश्चापहस्तोऽहं सरयूतीरमागतः। जिघांसुः श्वापदं किंचिनिपाने वागतं गजम्॥
translation: O revered one, desirous of killing some beast of prey, and elephant (or some other), come to the waters, I went to the banks of the Sarayū bow in hand.

sanskrit: ततः श्रुतो मया शब्दो जले कुम्भस्य पूर्यतः। द्विपोऽयमिति मत्वाहं बाणेनाभिहतो मया॥ गत्वा तस्यास्ततस्तीरमपश्यमिषुणा हृदि। विनिर्भिन्नं गतप्राणं शयानं भुवि तापसम्॥
translation: Then hearing sounds from the water of a filling pitcher, I thought, This must be an elephant. I wounded it with a shaft. Next coming to the edge of the river, I saw an ascetic lying down on the ground almost deprived of life, with his heart pierced with an arrow.

sanskrit: ततस्तस्यैव वचनादुपेत्य परितप्यतः। स मया सहसा बाण उद्धृतो ममतस्तदा॥
translation: Then coming forward, I in accordance with the direction given by him as he lay in agony, suddenly extracted the arrow from his vitals.

sanskrit: स चोद्धृतेन बाणेन सहसा स्वर्गमास्थितः। भगवन्तावुभौ शोचन्नन्धाविति विलप्य च॥
translation: And as soon as the arrow had been extracted, he ascended heaven, O reverend sir, lamenting and bewailing you, both grown old.

sanskrit: अज्ञानाद् भवतः पुत्रः सहसाभिहतो मया। शेषमेवं गते यत्स्यात् तत् प्रसीदतु मे मुनिः॥
translation: It is through ignorance that I suddenly wounded your son. This having been past, do you favour me with telling me what is now to be done, O ascetic.

sanskrit: स तच्छ्रुत्वा वचः क्रूरं मया तदघशंसिना। नाशकत् तीव्रमायासं स कर्तुं भगवानृषिः॥
translation: Having heard these cruel words, the worshipful ascetic could well by his curse consume me to ashes.

sanskrit: स बाष्पपूर्णवदनो निःश्वसशोकमूर्च्छितः। मामुवाच महातेजाः कृताञ्जलिमुपस्थितम्॥
translation: With eyes flooded with tears, and well nigh deprived of his senses by grief, that highly energetic one said to me standing with joined hands.

sanskrit: यद्येतदशुभं कर्म न स्म मे कथयेः स्वयम्। फलेन्मूर्धा स्म राजन् सद्यः शतसहस्रधा॥
translation: If, O king, you had not of yourself immediately communicated to us this unpleasant news, your head would have been reduced to a thousand flaws.

sanskrit: क्षत्रियेण वधो राजन् वानप्रस्थे विशेषतः। ज्ञानपूर्वं कृतः स्थानाच्च्यावयेदपि वज्रिणम्॥
translation: Not to speak of Kștriyas, I can even drag the very wielder of the thunderbolt himself from his position, if he knowingly kills one, in especial, that has assumed the Vånaprastha mode of life.

sanskrit: सप्तधा तु भवेन्मूर्धा मुनौ तपसि तिष्ठति। ज्ञानाद् विसृजतः शस्त्रं तादृशे ब्रह्मवादिनि॥
translation: Your head would have been severed in seven, if you had discharged the weapon knowingly at such an ascetic staying in austerities and versed in the Vedas.

sanskrit: अज्ञानाद्धि कृतं यस्मादिदं ते तेन जीवसे। अपि ह्यकुशलं न स्याद् राघवाणां कुतोभवान् ॥
translation: It is because you have done this through ignorance that you (still) live, else the race itself of the Rāghavas should be not, and where are you?

sanskrit: ते नय नौ नृप तं देशमिति मां चाभ्यभाषत। अद्य तं द्रष्टुमिच्छावः पुत्रं पश्चिमदर्शनम्॥
translation: He then said, 'Do you, o king, take us to the scene. To day will we look our last on our son besmeared with blood, his deer-skin garb falling off (from his body), lying senseless on the earth, and come under the subjection of the lord of righteousness.'

sanskrit: रुधिरेणावसिक्ताङ्गं प्रकीर्णाजिनवाससम्। शयानं भुवि निःसंज्ञं धर्मराजवशं गतम्॥ अथाहमेकस्तं देशं नीत्वा तौ भृशदुःखितौ। अस्पर्शयमहं पुत्रं तं मुनि सह भार्यया॥
translation: Thereupon I alone taking them exceedingly disconsolate to the spot, made the ascetic and his wife touch their son.

sanskrit: तौ पुत्रमात्मनः स्पृष्ट्वा तमासाद्य तपस्विनौ। निपेततुः शरीरेऽस्य पिता चैनमुवाच ह॥
translation: And having approached their son and touched him, ascetics fell on his person, and then his father addressed him thus.

sanskrit: नाभिवादयसे माऽद्य न च मामभिभाषसे। किं च शेषे तु भूमौ त्वं वत्स किं कुपितो ह्यसि।।३०।
translation: You salute me not to-day, nor did you speak to me. Why, my child, did you lie down on the ground? Art you angry (with us)?

sanskrit: नन्वहं तेऽप्रियः पुत्र मातरं पश्य धार्मिकीम्। किं च नालिङ्गसे पुत्र सुकुमार वचो वद॥
translation: If, my son, you do not feel kindly to me, do you look up to your virtuous mother. And why, O son, do you not embrace me? Do you speak tender words.

sanskrit: कस्य वा पररात्रेऽहं श्रोष्यामि हृदयङ्गमम्। अधीयानस्य मधुरं शास्त्रं वान्यद् विशेषतः॥
translation: At the small hours, form whom engaged in study, shall I hear the scriptures sweetly read in a way coming home to the listener's mind?

sanskrit: को मां संध्यामुपास्यैव स्नात्वा हुतहुताशनः। श्लाघयिष्यत्युपासीनः पुत्रशोकभयादितम् ॥
translation: Who, having performed his daily devotions and offered oblation to the sacrificial fire, will bathe me, afflicted with grief for my son?

sanskrit: कन्दमूलफलं हृत्वा यो मां प्रियमिवातिथिम्। भोजयिष्यत्यकर्मण्यमप्रग्रहमनायकम्॥
translation: Who procuring Kandas, fruits and roots, will feed me like an welcome guest, incapable of and doing anything and furnishing provisions, and without any one to take care of myself.?

sanskrit: इमामन्धां च वृद्धां च मातरं ते तपस्विनीम्। कथं पुत्र भरिष्यामि कृपणां पुत्रगर्धिनीम्॥
translation: And, my son, how will I maintain this blind ascetic mother of yours, proud of her son, who is passing her days in misery?

sanskrit: तिष्ठ मा मा गमः पुत्र यमस्य सदनं प्रति। श्वो मया सह गन्तासि जनन्या च समेधितः॥
translation: Do you stay my son, in my behalf. Tomorrow you will go to Yama's mansion with me and your mother.

sanskrit: उभावपि च शोकार्तावनाथौ कृपणौ वने। क्षिप्रमेव गमिष्यावस्त्वया हीनौ यमक्षयम्॥
translation: Distressed with grief and rendered miserable in the forest, both of us deprived of you shall soon repair to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: ततो वैवस्वतं दृष्ट्वा तं प्रवक्ष्यामि भारतीम्। क्षमतां धर्मराजो मे बिभृयात् पितरावयम्॥
translation: Seeing Vivasvata's son, I will say to him, Do you, O lord of justice forgive me, and let this my son, continue to maintain us, his parents.

sanskrit: दातुमर्हति धर्मात्मा लोकपालो महायशाः। ईदृशस्य ममाक्षय्यामेकामभयदक्षिणाम्॥
translation: It behove you, O righteous and illustrious guardian of the words, to confer on me reduced to such a pass this one enduring dakşiņā capable of removing our fear.

sanskrit: अपापोऽसि यथा पुत्र निहतः पापकर्मणा। तेन सत्येन गच्छाशु ये लोकास्त्वस्त्रयोधिनाम्॥ यां हि शूरा गतिं यान्ति संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनः। हतास्त्वभिमुखाः पुत्र गतिं तां परमां व्रज॥
translation: You, my son, are sinless, although slain by this one who has done an unrighteous act; and by the force of this truth , do you repair to the world of warriors. Do you, O son, go the supreme way that is gone by heroes who without turning back from the fight, are slain in open encounter.

sanskrit: यां गतिं सगरः शैब्यो दिलीपो जनमेजयः। नहुषो धुन्धुमारश्च प्राप्तास्तां गच्छ पुत्रक॥
translation: Do you, O son, go the way that has been gone by Sagara and Saivya and Dilīpa and Janamejaya and Nahusa and Dhundhumāra.

sanskrit: या गतिः सर्वभूतानां स्वाध्यायात् तपसश्च या। भूमिदस्याहिताग्नेश्च एकपत्नीव्रतस्य च ॥ गोसहस्रप्रदातॄणां गुरुसेवाभृतामपि। देहन्यासकृतां या च तां गतिं गच्छ पुत्रक॥
translation: Do you, O son, go the way that is gone by all creatures, even by ascetics engaged in the study of the Veda, by bestowers of lands, by those performing fire-sacrifices, by individuals each devoted to a single wife, men giving away a thousand kine, persons tending their preceptors, and individuals renouncing lives by fasting.

sanskrit: न हि त्वस्मिन् कुले जातो गच्छत्यकुशलां गतिम्। स तु यास्यति येन त्वं निहतो मम बान्धवः॥
translation: He that is born in such a race cannot come by any evil case. Such a condition be his that has taken the life of you, my friend.'

sanskrit: एवं स कृपणं तत्र पर्यदेवयतासकृत्। तथोक्त्वा कर्तुमुदकं प्रवृत्तः सह भार्यया॥
translation: Having thus piteously wept, he along with his wife set about performing the watery rites on behalf of his son.

sanskrit: स तु दिव्येन रूपेण मुनिपुत्रः स्वकर्मभिः। स्वर्गमध्यारुहत् क्षिप्रं शक्रेण सह धर्मवित्॥
translation: Thereupon speedily assuming a celestial shape, the virtuous son of the ascetic by his own actions ascended heaven in company with Sakra.

sanskrit: आबभाषे च तौ वृद्धौ शक्रेण सह तापसः। आश्वस्य च मुहूर्तं तु पितरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Then (returning) along with Sakra, the ascetic comforting his aged parents, addressed them, sa ing.

sanskrit: स्थानमस्मि महत् प्राप्तो भवतोः परिचारणात्। भवन्तावपि च क्षिप्रं मम मूलमुपैष्यथः॥
translation: I have attained a high state in consequence of having served you. Do you also without delay come to me.

sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तु दिव्येन विमानेन वपुष्मता। मामुवाच महातेजाः आरुरोह दिवं क्षिप्रं मुनिपुत्रो जितेन्द्रियः॥
translation: Having said this, the ascetic's son of restrained sense ascended heaven by means of an excellent and commodious car.

sanskrit: स कृत्वाथोदकं तूर्णं तापसः सह भार्यया। कृताञ्जलिमुपस्थितम्॥
translation: Having performed the watery rites, the highly energetic ascetic along with his wife speedily said to me staying with joined hands.

sanskrit: अद्यैव जहि मां राजन् मरणे नास्ति मे व्यथा। यः शरेणैकपुत्रं मां त्वमकार्षीरपुत्रकम्॥
translation: Do you, O monarch, slay me on the instant. I do not grieve to die', you have by your shaft rendered me who had an only son, absolutely sonless.

sanskrit: त्वयापि च यदज्ञानानिहतो मे स बालकः। तेन त्वामपि शप्स्येऽहं सुदुःखमतिदारुणम्॥ पुत्रव्यसनजं दुःखं यदेतन्मम साम्प्रतम्। एवं त्वं पुत्रशोकेन राजन् कालं करिष्यसि ॥
translation: Since this sorrow arising from the calamity that has befallen my son, is at present mine (through your instrumentality), I curse you. You shall even in this way find your death from grief born of separation from your son.

sanskrit: अज्ञानात्तु हतो यस्मात् क्षत्रियेण त्वया मुनिः। तस्मात् त्वां नाविशत्याशु ब्रह्महत्या नराधिप॥ त्वामप्येतादृशो भावः क्षिप्रमेव गमिष्यति। जीवितान्तकरो घोरो दातारमिव दक्षिणाम्॥
translation: As you a Kşatriya has through ignorance slain an ascetic, the sin, O lord of men, of slaying a Brāhmaṇa will not envelope you speedily; but you shall shortly come by this dreadful and mortal condition, like a donor of Dakşiņās (coming by the things given away).'

sanskrit: एवं शापं मयि न्यस्य विलप्य करुणं बहु। चितामारोप्य देहं तन्मिथुनं स्वर्गमभ्ययात्॥
translation: Having thus inflicted on me the curse and piteously lamented long, the coupe ascended the funeral pile and went to heaven.

sanskrit: तदेतच्चिन्तयानेन स्मृतं पापं मया स्वयम्। तदा बाल्यात् कृतं देवि शब्दवेध्यनुकर्षिणा॥
translation: O noble dame, the crime that I hitting by help of sound, had committed in my boyhood, has reverted to my recollection in course of thought.

sanskrit: तस्यायं कर्मणो देवि विपाकः समुपस्थितः। अपथ्यैः सह सम्भुक्ते व्याधिरनरसे यथा॥ तस्मान्मामागतं भद्रे तस्योदारस्य तद् वचः।
translation: O exalted lady, even as a disease generated by one's taking rice with unhealthy curry, this danger is imminent in consequence of that act. O gentle one, the words of that noble-minded person are about to be verified in me.

sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा स रुदंस्त्रस्तो भार्यामाह तु भूमिपः॥ यदहं पुत्रशोकेन संत्यजिष्यामि जीवितम्। चक्षुभ्यां त्वां न पश्यामि कौसल्ये त्वं हि मां स्पृश।।
translation: Having said this and weeping, the king said to his wife, “I shall renounce life through grief for my son. And I shall no more behold you with my eyes. Do you, O Kausalyā, touch me."

sanskrit: यमक्षयमनुप्राप्ता द्रक्ष्यन्ति नहि मानवाः। यदि मां संस्पृशेद् रामः सकृदन्वारभेत वा॥
translation: People going to the mansion of Yama no more behold (their friends): If Rama touch me directly or otherwise, obtain the exchequer, and be installed as the heir-apparent, Meseems, I may yet live.

sanskrit: धनं वा यौवराज्यं वा जीवेयमिति मे मतिः। न तन्मे सदृशं देवि यन्मया राघवे कृतम्॥ सदृशं तत्तु तस्यैव यदनेन कृतं मयि।
translation: O noble lady, what I have done to Rāghava in not surely like myself; but what (on the other hand) he has done by me is worthy of him.

sanskrit: दुर्वृत्तमपि कः पुत्रं त्यजेद् भुवि विचक्षणः॥ कश्च प्रव्राज्यमानो वा नासूयेत् पितरं सुतः।
translation: What sensible man for sake his son, albeit he may be wicked? And what son being banished, does not bear ill will towards his father?

sanskrit: चक्षुषा त्वां न पश्यामि स्मृतिर्मम विलुप्यते॥ दूता वैवस्वतस्यैते कौसल्ये त्वरयन्ति माम्।
translation: But I do not see you with my eyes, and my memory fails. These envoys of Vivasvata's son, OKausalya, urge speed upon me.

sanskrit: अतस्तु किं दुःखतरं यदहं जीवितक्षये॥ नहि पश्यामि धर्मज्ञं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्।
translation: What can be an object of greater regret than that I during my last moments cannot behold the righteous Rāma having truth for prowess?

sanskrit: तस्य दर्शनजः शोकः सुतस्याप्रतिकर्मणः॥ उच्छोषयति वै प्राणान् वारि स्तोकमिवातपः।
translation: Even as the sun dried up a drop of water, grief for not seeing my son of incomparable acts dried my spirits.

sanskrit: न ते मनुष्या देवास्ते ये चारुशुभकुण्डलम्॥ मुखं द्रक्ष्यन्ति रामस्य वर्षे पञ्चदशे पुनः।
translation: Those are not men, those are gods who in the fifteenth year shall again behold Rāma's countenance graced with elegant and burnished ear-rings.

sanskrit: पद्मपत्रेक्षणं सुभ्र सुदंष्ट्रं चारुनासिकम्॥ धन्या द्रक्ष्यन्ति रामस्य ताराधिपसमं मुखम्।
translation: O you of graceful eye-brows, blessed are they who shall behold Rāma's countenance furnished with eyes resembling lotus-petals, with excellent teeth and a shapely nose, like to the lord of the stars himself.

sanskrit: सदृशं शारदस्येन्दोः फुल्लस्य कमलस्य च॥ सुगन्धि मम रामस्य धन्या द्रक्ष्यन्ति ये मुखम्। निवृत्तवनवासं तमयोध्यां पुनरागतम्॥ द्रक्ष्यन्ति सुखिनो रामं शुक्रं मार्गगतं तथा।
translation: Blessed are they that shall behold that fragrant face of his like to the autumnal moon, or the fullblown lotus. Thrice-blessed they who with delighted hearts, shall behold Rāma returned from the forest and come back to Ayodhyā, like to Sukra crowning the zenith?

sanskrit: कौसल्ये चित्तमोहेन हृदयं सीदतेतराम्॥ वेदये न च संयुक्ताशब्दस्पर्शरसानहम्। चित्तनाशाद् विपद्यन्ते सर्वाण्येवेन्द्रियाणि हि। क्षीणस्नेहस्य दीपस्य संरक्ता रश्मयो यथा॥
translation: O Kausalyā, my heart is weighed down with grief; and I do not perceive objects of hearing, feeling, or taste. My senses are growing dim in consequence of the mental stupor, like the rays of a lamp reduced to smoke, becoming dim when the oil has been exhausted.

sanskrit: अयमात्मभवः शोको मामनाथमचेतनम्। संसाधयति वेगेन यथा कूलं नदीरयः॥
translation: As the violence of a river wears away its banks, my grief occasioned through my own agency is destroying me, who am helpless and insensible.

sanskrit: हा राघव महाबाहो हा ममायासनाशन। हा पितृप्रिय मे नाथ हा ममासि गतः सुत । ७५ ।।
translation: O mighty-armed Rāghava! O you remover of my troubles! O you that do delight in your father! you are my stay, O my son, that have gone away.

sanskrit: हा कौसल्ये न पश्यामि हा सुमित्रे तपस्विनि। हा नृशंसे ममामित्रे कैकेयि कुलपांसनि॥
translation: O Kausalyā, I do not see. O wretched Sumitrā! O cruel one, you enemy of mine, you Kaikeyī, who have befouled your line!

sanskrit: इति मातुश्च रामस्य सुमित्रायाश्च संनिधौ। राजा दशरथः शोचञ्जीवितान्तमुपागमत्॥
translation: Having thus lamented in presence of Rāma's mother and Sumitrā, king Daſaratha breathed his last.

sanskrit: तथा तु दीनः कथयन् नराधिपः प्रियस्य पुत्रस्य विवासनातुरः। स्तदा जहौ प्राणमुदारदर्शनः। ७८ ।।
translation: Thus that distressed lord of men, smitten with 1e exile of his beloved son, that one possessed fa gracious presence, when the night had been alf spent, wrought up with the violence of his notion, departed this life.

sanskrit: आक्रन्दिता निरानन्दा सास्रकण्ठजनाविला। अयोध्यायामवतता सा व्यतीयाय शर्वरी॥
translation: At length the weary night in Ayodhya rendered cheerless cheerless by lamentations, and populous with men with voice choked with tears, was spent.

sanskrit: व्यतीतायां तु शर्वर्यामादित्यस्योदये ततः। समेत्य राजकर्तारः सभामीयुर्द्विजातयः॥ मार्कण्डेयोऽथ मौद्गल्यो वामदेवश्च कश्यपः। कात्यायनो गौतमश्च जाबालिश्च महायशाः॥ एते द्विजाः सहामात्यैः पृथग्वाचमुदीरयन्। वसिष्ठमेवाभिमुखाः श्रेष्ठं राजपुरोहितम्॥
translation: And when the night had departed and the sun had arisen, those officers of the royal house-hold belonging to the twice-born order, Märkandeya, Maudgalya, Vāmadeva, Kaśyapa, Kātyāyana, Gautama, and the highly famous Jābāli. assembled together along with the counsellors, spoke each on different topics.

sanskrit: अतीता शर्वरी दुःखं या नो वर्षशतोपमा। अस्मिन् पञ्चत्वमापने पुत्रशोकेन पार्थिवे॥
translation: Then facing the royal priest, the eminent Vasistha, they said, "That night that had appeared like to an hundred years has at last been painfully passed.

sanskrit: स्वर्गस्थश्च महाराजो रामश्चारण्यमाश्रितः। लक्ष्मणश्चापि तेजस्वी रामेपैव गतः सह॥ उभौ भरतशत्रुघ्नौ केकयेषु परंतपौ। पुरे राजगृहे रम्ये मातामहनिवेशने॥
translation: The king racked by sorrow for his son having breathed his last, the mighty monarch has ascended heaven, Rāma has taken refuge in the woods, the energetic Lakşmaņa has gone with Rama, and does Bharata and Satrughna, repressors of foes, are staying in Kekaya in pleasant Rājagrha, the abode of their maternal grandfather.

sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकूणामिहाद्यैव कश्चिद् राजा विधीयताम्। अराजकं हि नो राष्ट्र विनाशं समवाप्नुयात् ।।८
translation: Do you select some on this very day from the descendants of Ikşvāku, to be king here. Verily does a kingdom go to ruin, when without a king.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे विद्युन्माली महास्वनः। अभिवर्षति पर्जन्यो महीं दिव्येन वारिणा॥
translation: He that goes garlanded with lightning, and has a mighty voice, even the Cloud, does not with Skye shower drench the Earth in a kingdom without a king.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे बीजमुष्टिः प्रकीर्यते। अराजके पितुः पुत्रो भार्या वा वर्तते वशे॥
translation: In a kingless kingdom no one sows corn. In a kingless kingdom the son does not obey his sire, or the wife her husband.

sanskrit: अराजके धनं नास्ति नास्ति भार्याप्यराजके। इदमत्याहितं चान्यत् कुतः सत्यमराजके॥
translation: A kingless kingdom possesses no wealth, and wives are hard to keep in such a place. This great fear attends a kingless country. And where is other morality (besides that detailed above) to be found at such a place?

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे कारयन्ति सभां नराः। उद्यानानि च रम्याणि हृष्टाः पुण्यगृहाणि च॥
translation: In a kingless country men do not form themselves into associations, nor do they, inspired with cheerfulness, make elegant gardens or sacred edifices.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे यज्ञशीला द्विजातयः। सत्राण्यन्वासते दान्ता ब्राह्मणाः संशितव्रताः॥ नाराजके जनपदे महायज्ञेषु यज्वनः। ब्राह्मणा वसुसम्पूर्णा विसृजन्त्याप्तदक्षिणाः॥
translation: In a kingless country, the twice-born ones do not celebrate sacrifices. In a kingless country, in mighty sacrifices wealthy Brāhmaṇas do not confer (on the officiating priests) the Dakșiņās (which they receive according to the ordinance).

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे प्रहृष्टनटनर्तकाः। उत्सवाश्च समाजाश्च वर्धन्ते राष्ट्रवर्धनाः॥
translation: In a kingless country, neither neither social gatherings, nor festivities characterised by the presence of merry theatrical managers and performers, increase.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे सिद्धार्था व्यवहारिणः। कथाभिरभिरज्यन्ते कथाशीलाः कथाप्रियैः॥
translation: In a kingless country disputants cannot decide their point; nor are persons given to hearing Puranic recitations pleased by those delighting in the practice.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे तूद्यानानि समागताः। सायाह्ने क्रीडितुं यान्ति कुमार्यो हेमभूषिताः॥
translation: In a kingless country, bevies of virgins decked in gold do not repair to gardens for purposes of sport.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे धनवन्तः सुरक्षिताः। शेरते विवृतद्वाराः कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः॥
translation: In a kingless country, the wealthy are not well protected; nor do shepherds and cultivators sleep with their doors open.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे वाहनैः शीघ्रवाहिभिः। नरा निर्यान्त्यरण्यानि नारीभिः सह कामिनः॥
translation: In a kingless country pleasure-seeking people do not in company with females go to the woods by means of swift vehicles.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे बद्धघण्टा विषाणिनः। अटन्ति राजमार्गेषु कुञ्जराः षष्ठिहायनाः॥
translation: In a kingless country long-tusked elephants sixty years old, bearing bells on their necks, do not walk the high-way.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे शरान् संततमस्यताम्। श्रूयते तलनिर्घोष इष्वस्त्राणामुपासने॥
translation: In a kingless country one hears not the clappings of persons engaged in shooting arrows constantly.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे वणिजो दूरगामिनः। गच्छन्ति क्षेममध्वानं बहुपण्यसमाचिताः॥
translation: In a kingless country traders coming from distant lands, loaded with various kinds of merchandise, do not with safety go along the roads.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे चरत्येकचरो वशी। भावयन्नात्मनात्मानं यत्रसायं गृहो मुनिः॥
translation: In a kingless country the ascetic with his subdued senses, himself his sole protector, who makes his quarters wherever evening overtakes him, cannot walk contemplating the Deity.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे योगक्षेमः प्रवर्तते। न चाप्यराजके सेना शत्रून् विषहते युधि॥
translation: In a kingless country, one cannot protect what one has, or procure what one has not. In a kingless country, the forces cannot bear the onslaught of the foe.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे हृष्टैः परमवाजिभिः। नराः संयान्ति सहसा रथैश्च प्रतिमण्डिताः॥
translation: In a kingless country men cannot at will go on excellent and high-mettled horses and ornamented cars.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे नराः शास्त्रविशारदाः। संवदन्तोपतिष्ठन्ते वनेपूपवनेषु वा॥
translation: In a kingless country persons well versed in learning can not engage in controversy, repairing to woods and groves.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे माल्यमोदकदक्षिणाः। देवताभ्यर्चनार्थाय कल्प्यन्ते नियतैर्जनैः॥ नाराजके जनपदे चन्दनागुरुरुषिताः। राजपुत्रा विराजन्ते वसन्ते इव शाखिनः॥
translation: In a kingless country, persons with intent hearts do not offer garlands, sweets, and Daksinās, for worshipping the gods. In a kingless country princes smeared with sandal and aguru, do not look graceful like trees in spring.

sanskrit: यथा ह्यनुदका नद्यो यथा वाप्यतृणं वनम्। अगोपाला यथा गावस्तथा राष्ट्रमराजकम्॥
translation: Even as a river without water, a wood without grass, a herd of kine without a keeper, is a kingdom without a king.

sanskrit: ध्वजो रथस्य प्रज्ञानं धूमो ज्ञानं विभावसोः। तेषां यो नो ध्वजो राजा स देवत्वमितो गतः॥
translation: The sign of a car is its pennon, of fire is smoke, and our banner the king, has gone to heaven.

sanskrit: नाराजके जनपदे स्वकं भवति कस्यचित्। मत्स्या इव जना नित्यं भक्षयन्ति परस्परम्॥
translation: In a kingless country a person hardly preserves his life; and like fishes people eat up one another.

sanskrit: ये हि सम्भिन्नमर्यादा नास्तिकाश्छिन्नसंशयाः। तेऽपि भावाय कल्पन्ते राजदण्डनिपीडिताः॥
translation: Even those heretics who having disregarded the dignity of social morality had met with chastisement at the hands of the king, their fear removed, give themselves airs.

sanskrit: यथा दृष्टिः शरीरस्य नित्यमेव प्रवर्तते। तथा नरेन्द्रो राष्ट्रस्य प्रभवः सत्यधर्मयोः॥
translation: As the sight is engaged in the welfare of the body, the king, that fountain of truth and religion, is engaged in compassing the good of the kingdom.

sanskrit: राजा सत्यं च धर्मश्च राजा कुलवतां कुलम्। राजा माता पिता चैव राजा हितकारो नृणाम्॥
translation: The king is truth, the king is morality, the king is the racial dignity of those possessed of the same, the king is the father, the king is the ON 68 RĀMĀYAŅAM mother, the king compasses the welfare of men.

sanskrit: यमो वैश्रवणः शक्रो वरुणश्च महाबलः। विशिष्यन्ते नरेन्द्रेण वृत्तेन महता ततः॥
translation: By virtue of magnanimity of character, a king surpasses Yama and Vaiśravaṇa and Śakra and Varuņa endowed with mighty strength.

sanskrit: अहो तम इवेदं स्यान प्रज्ञायेत किंचन। राजा चेन भवेल्लोके विभजन् साध्वसाधुनी॥ जीवत्यपि महाराजे तवैव वचनं वयम्। नातिक्रमामहे सर्वे वेलां प्राप्येव सागः ॥
translation: If there were not a king in this world to adjudge fair and foul, darkness would overspread (the face of the earth) and people could not distinguish anything whatever. As the ocean keeps within its continent, we even while the monarch lived, did not disregard your words.

sanskrit: स नः समीक्ष्य द्विजवर्य वृत्तं नृपं विना राष्ट्रमरण्यभूतम्। कुमारमिक्ष्वाकुसुतं तथान्यं त्वमेव राजानमिहाभिषेचय॥
translation: Do you, O best of Brāhmaṇas, beholding our acts rendered nugatory, and this empire became a wilderness for want of a king, install that descendant of Ikşvāku or any other as king of this realm.

sanskrit: तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह। मित्रामात्यजनान् सर्वान् ब्राह्मणांस्तानिदं वचः॥
translation: Hearing their words, Vasiştha said to the Brāhmaṇas and the adherents and counsellors (of the king)

sanskrit: यदसौ मातुलकुले दत्तराज्यः परं सुखी। भरतो वसति भ्रात्रा शत्रुघ्नेन मुदान्वितः॥
translation: Bharata, on whom the king has conferred the kingdom, along with his brother Satrughna, is living happily in the house of his maternal uncle.

sanskrit: तच्छीघ्रं जवना दूता गच्छन्तु त्वरितं हयैः। आनेतुं भ्रातरौ वीरौ किं समीक्षामहे वयम्॥
translation: Let envoys by means of fleet coursers speedily repair thither and bring those heroic brothers. What shall we decide?

sanskrit: गच्छन्त्विति ततः सर्वे वसिष्ठं वाक्यमब्रुवन्। तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
translation: "Let them go", said all to Vasistha. Hearing their words, Vasistha spoke to them, saying.

sanskrit: एहि सिद्धार्थ विजय जयन्ताशोकनन्दन। श्रूयतामितिकर्तव्यं सर्वानेव ब्रवीमि वः॥
translation: Come here, you Siddhārtha, and Vijaya, and Jayanta, and Asokanandana. Do you hear. I well tell you what you are to do.

sanskrit: पुरं राजगृहं गत्वा शीघ्रं शीघ्रजवैर्हयैः। त्यक्तशोकैरिदं वाच्यः शासनाद् भरतो मम ॥
translation: First going speedily to the royal residence by means of swift horses, do you, renouncing grief, by my order speak these words of mine to Bharata.

sanskrit: पुरोहितस्त्वां कुशलं प्राह सर्वे च मन्त्रिणः। त्वरमाणश्च निर्याहि कृत्यमात्ययिकं त्वया।७॥
translation: The priest as well as the counsellors have enquired after your welfare. Do you at once set out. A business is at hand that brooks no delay on your part.

sanskrit: मा चास्मै प्रोषितं रामं मा चास्मै पितरं मृतम्। भवन्तः शंसिषुर्गत्वा राघवाणामितः क्षयम्॥
translation: But you must on no account communicate to him the exile of Rāma, or the demise of the monarch, or the destruction that has befallen the Raghu race through this occasion.

sanskrit: कौशेयानि च वस्त्राणि भूषणानि वराणि च। क्षिप्रमादाय राज्ञश्च भरतस्य च गच्छत॥
translation: Do you, speedily taking silk apparel and excellent ornaments for king Bharata, set off.

sanskrit: दत्तपथ्यशना दूता जग्मुः स्वं स्वं निवेशनम्। केकयांस्ते गमिष्यन्तो हयानारुह्य सम्मतान्॥
translation: Thereupon, having been furnished with the necessaries for the journey, they bound for Kekaya went to their respective abodes, mounted on goodly horses.

sanskrit: ततः प्रास्थानिकं कृत्वा कार्यशेषमनन्तरम्। वसिष्ठेनाभ्यनुज्ञाता दूताः संत्वरितं ययुः॥
translation: Then having supplied themselves with the necessaries of the journey, the envoys in consonance with Vasiştha's injunction, speedily went away.

sanskrit: न्यन्तेनापरतालस्य प्रलम्बस्योत्तरं प्रति। निषेवमाणास्ते जग्मुर्नदी मध्येन मालिनीम्॥
translation: Having proceeded by the west of Aparatāla, they in the middle crossed the Mālinſ, and went towards the north of Pralamba.

sanskrit: ते हास्तिनपुरे गङ्गां तीर्त्वा प्रत्यङ्मुखा ययुः। पाञ्चालदेशमासाद्य मध्येन कुरुजाङ्गलम्॥
translation: Then crossing the Gangā at Hastināpura, and arriving at Pāñcāla, they proceeded west ward through Kurujāngala.

sanskrit: सरांसि च सुफुल्लानि नदीश्च विमलोदकाः। निरीक्षमाणा जग्मुस्ते दूताः कार्यवशाद् द्रुतम्॥
translation: And beholding watery expan'ses filled with blown blossoms, and rivers containing pellucid waters, the envoys proceeded apace on account of the errand they had on hand.

sanskrit: ते प्रसन्नोदकां दिव्यां नानाविहगसेविताम्। उपातिजग्मुर्वेगेन शरदण्डां जलाकुलाम्॥
translation: And they darted past the Saradanda overflowing with delightful water, beautiful, and haunted by fowls of various kinds.

sanskrit: निकूलवृक्षमासाद्य दिव्यं सत्योपयाचनम्। अभिगम्याभिवाद्यं तं कुलिङ्गां प्राविशन् पुरीम्॥
translation: Then on the western bank of the stream, coming upon a tree called Satyopayācana presided by a deity, and bowing down to the tree and going round it, they entered the city of Kulinga.

sanskrit: अभिकालं ततः प्राप्य तेजोऽभिभवनाच्च्युताः। पितृपैतामहीं पुण्यां तेरुरिक्षुमती नदीम्॥
translation: And having passed Tejobhibhavana and arrived at Abhikāla, they crossed the sacred stream Ikşumatī belonging to the Ikşvākus for generations.

sanskrit: अवेक्ष्याञ्जलिपानांश्च ब्राह्मणान् वेदपारगान्। ययुर्मध्येन बाह्रीकान् सुदामानं च पर्वतम्॥
translation: Beholding here Brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas drinking water with their joined hands, they went through Vahllika towards the mount Sudaman.

sanskrit: विष्णोः पदं प्रेक्ष्यमाणा विपाशां चापि शाल्मलीम्। नदीर्वापीतटाकानि पल्वलानि सरांसि च॥ पश्यन्तो विविधांश्चापि सिंहान् व्याघ्रान् मृगान् द्विपान्। ययुः पथातिमहता शासनं भर्तुरीप्सवः॥
translation: There seeing the foot-print of Visnu, they desirous of doing the bidding of their master, proceeded a long way, viewing the Vipasa and the Salmali and rivers and tanks and pools and ponds and sheets of water and various kinds of lions and tigers and deer and elephants.

sanskrit: ते श्रान्तवाहना दूता विकृष्टेन सता पथा। गिरिव्रजं पुरवरं शीघ्रमासेदुरञ्जसा ॥
translation: And with their vehicles fatigued, the ambassadors, on account of the great distance of the way; speedily reached that best of cities, Girivraja.

sanskrit: भर्तुः प्रियार्थं कुलरक्षणार्थं भर्तुश्च वंशस्य परिग्रहार्थम्। अहेडमानास्त्वरया स्म दूता रात्र्यां तु ते तत्पुरमेव याताः॥
translation: And for pleasing their master, for the preservation of the people, and enabling Bharata to assume the reins of government, those envoys, casting aside negligence, swiftly entered the city in the night.

sanskrit: यामेव रात्रिं ते दूताः प्रविशन्ति स्म तां पुरीम्। भरतेनापि तां रात्रि स्वप्नो दृष्टोऽयमप्रियः॥
translation: The very same night that the envoys entered the city, Bharata saw an evil dream.

sanskrit: व्युष्टामेव तु तां रात्रिं दृष्ट्वा तं स्वप्नमप्रियम्। पुत्रो राजाधिराजस्य सुभृशं पर्यतप्यत॥
translation: And seeing that evil dream during the short hours, the son of that king of kings exceedingly burned in grief.

sanskrit: तप्यमानं तमाज्ञाय वयस्याः प्रियवादिनः। आयासं विनयिष्यन्तः सभायां चक्रिरे कथाः॥
translation: And finding him aggrieved, his sweet. speeched associates, endeavouring to chase the heaviness, began to converse on a variety of subjects.

sanskrit: वादयन्ति तदा शान्ति लासयन्त्यपि चापरे। नाटकान्यपरे स्माहुर्हास्यानि विविधानि च॥ ।
translation: Some played on instruments; some for the purpose of pacifying his mind, danced (the courtezans); others performed scenes variously fraught with the sentiment of mirth.

sanskrit: स तैर्महात्मा भरतः सखिभिः प्रियवादिभिः। गोष्ठीहास्यानि कुर्वद्भिर्न प्राहृष्यत राघवः॥
translation: But although his friends intending to ally his agitation set about enacting passages calculated to amuse family circles, that magnanimous descendant of Raghu did not indulge in laughter.

sanskrit: तमब्रवीत् प्रियसखो भरतं सखिभिर्वृतम्। सुहृद्भिः पर्युपासीनः किं सखे नानुमोदसे॥
translation: Then a dear friend addressed Bharata, as he sat surrounded by his friends, “Surrounded by your friends, why do you not, my friend, join in the mirth?"

sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवाणं सुहृदं भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह। शृणु त्वं यनिमित्तं मे दैन्यमेतदुपागतम्॥ स्वप्ने पितरमद्राक्षं मलिनं मुक्तमूर्धजम्। पतन्तमद्रिशिखरात् कलुषे गोमये हृदे॥
translation: Thus asked by his friend, Bharata answered, “Listen why this depression has overtaken me. In a dream I beheld my father, pale, with his hair loosely flowing about, plunging from the summit of a mountain into a dirty pool filled with cowdung.”

sanskrit: प्लवमानश्च मे दृष्टः स तस्मिन् गोमये हृदे। पिबन्नञ्जलिना तैलं हसन्निव मुहुर्मुहुः॥
translation: And I saw him floating on a sink of cowdung, and yet with a momentary laugh drinking oil by means of his joined hands.

sanskrit: ततस्तिलोदनं भुक्त्वा पुनः पुनरधःशिराः। तैलेनाभ्यक्तसर्वाङ्गस्तैलमेवान्वगाहत॥
translation: Then feeding on rice mixed with sesame, he again and again hanging his head down, dives into oil with his limbs rubbed with oil.

sanskrit: स्वप्नेऽपि सागरं शुष्कं चन्द्रं च पतितं भुवि। उपरुद्धां च जगतीं तमसेव समावृताम्॥ औपवाह्यस्य नागस्य विषाणं शकलीकृतम्। सहसा चापि संशान्ता ज्वलिता जातवेदसः॥ अवदीर्णां च पृथिवीं शुष्कांश्च विविधान् दुमान् । अहं पश्यामि विध्वस्तान् सधूमांश्चैव पर्वतान्॥
translation: And in my dream I saw the ocean dried up, and the moon fallen on the earth, and the earth as if invaded by enfolding darkness, and the tusk of the elephant on which the monarch rides falling in fragments, and flaming fire suddenly extinguished, and the earth rent, and the trees withered, and all the mountains belching smoke.

sanskrit: पीठे कार्णायसे चैव निषण्णं कृष्णवाससम्। प्रहरन्ति स्म राजानं प्रमदाः कृष्णपिङ्गलाः॥
translation: I saw the king seated on a sable seat of iron, clad in a sable garb; and women black and yellow beating him.

sanskrit: त्वरमाणश्च धर्मात्मा रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः। रथेन खरयुक्तेन प्रयार्ता दक्षिणामुखः॥
translation: And bearing a garland of red flowers, with his body daubed with red sandal, he was fast proceeding to the south in a car yoked with asses.

sanskrit: प्रहसन्तीव राजानं प्रमदा रक्तवासिनी। प्रकर्षन्ती मया दृष्टा राक्षसी विकृतानना॥
translation: And women clad in red garment were laughing at him, and a grim-visaged Rākşasa was seen by me as dragging him.

sanskrit: एवमेतन्मया दृष्टमिमां रात्रिं भयावहाम्। अहं रामोऽथवा राजा लक्ष्मणो वा मरिष्यति॥
translation: This was the dream that I saw this terrible night. Either I, or Rama, or the king, or Lakşmaņa is to breathe our last.

sanskrit: नरो यानेन यः स्वप्ने खरयुक्तेन याति हि। अचिरात्तस्य धूम्राग्रं चितायां सम्प्रदृश्यते॥ एतन्निमित्तं दीनोऽहं न वचः प्रतिपूजये। शुष्यतीव च मे कण्ठो न स्वस्थमिव मे मनः॥
translation: The smoke of the funeral pyre of him will be shortly visible that goes in the car yoked with asses. It is for this reason that I am poor of spirit, and that I do not respond to your words. Further, my throat is parched, and my mind ill at ease.

sanskrit: न पश्यामि भयस्थानं भयं चैवोपधारये। भ्रष्टश्च स्वरयोगो मे छाया चापगता मम। जुगुप्सु इव चात्मानं न च पश्यामि कारणम्॥
translation: Ground of fear find I none, yet am I subject to fear. My voice is untuned, and my grace fled, and I begin to despise my life, nor know I the reason why.

sanskrit: इमां च दुःस्वप्नगतिं निशम्य हि त्वनेकरूपामवितर्कितां पुरा। भयं महत्वद् हृदयान याति मे विचिन्त्य राजानमचिन्त्यदर्शनम्॥
translation: Bringing to mind this various-looking dream which I had not thought of before, and remembering the king of incomprehensible presence, this fear goes not from my heart.

sanskrit: स प्राङ्मुखो राजगृहादभिनिर्याय वीर्यवान्। ततः सुदामां द्युतिमान् संतीर्यावेक्ष्य तां नदीम्॥ ह्रादिनी दूरपारं च प्रत्यक्स्रोतस्तरङ्गिणीम्। शतद्रुमतरच्छीमान् नदीमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः॥
translation: Issuing from the palace, the blazing Bharata endowed with prowess went in an easterly direction, and seeing before him the river called Sudāmā, crossed it. Then the auspicious descendant of Iksvāku crossed the broad Hrādinſ coursing westwards, as also the river Satadru.
