sanskrit: ऐलधाने नदीं तीर्वा प्राप्य चापरपर्वतान्। शिलामाकुर्वती ती। आग्नेयं शल्यकर्षणम्॥
translation: Then crossing a river at Eladhana,' and coming to Aparaparvata”, he crossed the Sila? and the Akurvatī, and arrived at Agneya* and Salyakarsanam. 1. Some read Eladhani. 2. Some read Apharaparyata. 3. The river, according to some is so named because it transforms the surrounding objects to stone. 4. Some make Agneya an epithet to Salyakarsana, meaning, relating to the south-east.

sanskrit: सत्यसंधः शुचिर्भूत्वा प्रेक्षमाणः शिलावहाम्। अभ्यगात् स महाशैलान् वनं चैत्ररथं प्रति ॥
translation: And having purified himself and seen Silavaha,' that one of truthful purposes passed the Mahacailas,' and entered the forest of Caitraratha. 1. According to Tirtha, Silavaha is a strcam having Āgneya on one side and Salyakarşaņa on the other. 2. Lit, mighty mountains.

sanskrit: सरस्वतीं च गङ्गां च युग्मेन प्रतिपद्य च। उत्तरान् वीरमत्स्यानां भारुण्डं प्राविशद् वनम्॥
translation: Then coming upon the confluence of the Ganga and the Sarasvati, Bharata entered the forest of Bhārunda lying to the north* of Vīramatsya. *Uttarān, lit. north. Some text read uttaram. It would mean countries lying to the north of Viramatsya.

sanskrit: वेगिनी च कुलिङ्गाख्यां ह्रादिनी पर्वतावृताम्। यमुनां प्राप्य संतीर्णो बलमाश्वासयत् तदा॥
translation: Next crossing the rapid river Kulingā and the Hrādinſ surrounded by hills, as well as the Yamunā, he ordered the forces to halt.

sanskrit: शीतीकृत्वा तु गात्राणि क्लान्तानाश्वास्य वाजिनः। तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च प्रायादादाय चोदकम्॥ राजपुत्रो महारण्यमनभीक्ष्णोपसेवितम्। भद्रो भद्रेण यानेन मारुतः खमिवात्यगात्॥
translation: Then cooling the limbs of the fatigued horses (with water) and refreshing them, Bharata himself bathed there and drank of the water; and then resumed the march, furnished with the water. Then the gentle prince by means of an excellent car, like to the wind-god himself, entered the mighty forest inhabited by various races of men.

sanskrit: भागीरथी दुष्प्रतरां सोंऽशुधाने महानदीम्। उपायात् राघवस्तूर्णं प्राग्वटे विश्रुते पुरे॥
translation: Seeing that the mighty river Gangā was hard to cross at Ansudhāna, Bharata speedily went to the famous city of Prāgvața.

sanskrit: स गङ्गां प्राग्वटे ती, समायात् कुटिकोष्ठिकाम्। सबलस्तां स तीथि समगाद् धर्मवर्धनम्॥
translation: Having crossed the Gangă at Prāgvața, he went over to the Kuţikoșthika. Having with his forces crossed that river, he proceeded to Dharmavardhana.

sanskrit: तोरणं दक्षिणार्धेन जम्बूप्रस्थं समागमत्। वरूथं च ययौ रम्यं ग्रामं दशरथात्मजः॥
translation: Then proceeding by the south of Toraņa, he came to Jambuprastha. Then Dasaratha's son went to the beautiful village of Varūtha.

sanskrit: तत्र रम्ये वने वासं कृत्वासौ प्राङ्मुखो ययौ। उद्यानमुज्जिहानायाः प्रियका यत्र पादपाः॥
translation: Having for a while stayed at that romantic wood, he proceeded eastwards, and presented himself at the villa of Ujjihānāya, where abound trees (called) Priyaka.

sanskrit: स तांस्तु प्रियकान् प्राप्य शीघ्रानास्थाय वाजिनः। अनुज्ञाप्याथ भरतो वाहिनीं त्वरितो ययौ॥
translation: Coming to the Priyakas, Bharata speedily yoking the horses, set out without delay, issuing his orders to the forces.

sanskrit: वासं कृत्वा सर्वतीर्थे ती चोत्तानिकां नदीम्। अन्या नदीश्च विविधैः पार्वतीयैस्तुरङ्गमैः॥ हस्तिपृष्ठकमासाद्य कुटिकामप्यवर्तत। ततार च नरव्याघ्रो लोहित्ये च कपीवतीम्॥ एकसाले स्थाणुमती विनते गोमती नदीम्। कलिङ्गनगरे चापि प्राप्य सालवनं तदा ॥ भरतः क्षिप्रमागच्छत् सुपरिश्रान्तवाहनः। वनं च समतीत्याशु शर्वर्यामरुणोदये॥ अयोध्यां मनुना राज्ञा निर्मितां स ददर्श ह। तां पुरी पुरुषव्याघ्रः सप्तरात्रोषितः पथि॥
translation: Then sojourning at Sarvatirtha and crossing the river there flowing north-wards as well as others abounding in various kinds of mountainous horses, Bharata arrived Hastiprşthaka. And at Lohitya that foremost of men crossed the Kapivati, at Ekasāla, the Sthanumati, and at Vinaya the Gomati. And Bharata arriving at a forest of Sala trees in the city of Kalinga, speedily passed it with his forces way-worn. And having passed the forest swiftly over night, he at sunrise saw Ayodhyā built by king Manu. Having spent seven nights on the journey, that chief of men beheld Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: अयोध्यामग्रतो दृष्ट्वा सारथिं चेदमब्रवीत्। एषा नातिप्रतीता मे पुण्योद्याना यशस्विनी॥ अयोध्या दृश्यते दूरात् सारथे पाण्डुमृत्तिका। यज्विभिर्गुणसम्पन्नैर्ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः॥ भूयिष्ठमृद्धैराकीर्णा राजर्षिवरपालिता। अयोध्यायां पुरा शब्दः श्रूयते तुमुलो महान्॥ समन्तानरनारीणां तमद्य न शृणोम्यहम्।
translation: Before him and thus addressed the charioteer, O charioteer, from the distance Ayodhyā at seemeth like a mass of black earth, albeit she boasts of sacrificial priests crowned with every virtue, Brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas and opulent people, and albeit she is maintained by Rājarșis. Formerly one could hear a great and mighty tumult all round Ayodhyā proceeding from men and women; but I do not hear this today.

sanskrit: उद्यानानि हि सायाह्ने क्रीडित्वोपरतैनरैः॥ समन्ताद् विप्रधावद्भिः प्रकाशन्ते ममान्यथा। तान्यद्यानुरुदन्तीव परित्यक्तानि कामिभिः॥
translation: The gardens where from persons having sported in the evening used to rush out (at day break) wear a different aspect now. Forsaken by the pleasure-seekers, the garden appear to weep.

sanskrit: अरण्यभूतेव पुरी सारथे प्रतिभाति माम्। सह्यत्र यानैर्दृश्यन्ते न गर्न च वाजिभिः। निर्यान्तो वाभियान्तो वा नरमुख्या यथा पुरा॥
translation: O charioteer, the city appears to me like a wilderness. And I do not as formerly behold the flower of the city leaving or entering her on cars or elephants or horses.

sanskrit: उद्यानानि पुरा भान्ति मत्तप्रमुदितानि च। जनानां रतिसंयोगेष्वत्यन्तगुणवन्ति च॥ तान्येतान्यद्य पश्यामि निरानन्दानि सर्वशः। स्रस्तपर्णैरनुपथं विक्रोशद्भिरिव दुमैः॥
translation: Gardens which, frequented by people inebriated with the honey of love, met together for purposes of sport, looked charmingly blooming, I find as utterly void of cheerfulness, with the trees as if lamenting with tremulous leaves.

sanskrit: नाद्यापि श्रूयते शब्दो मत्तानां मृगपक्षिणाम्। सरक्तां मधुरां वाणी कलं व्याहरतां बहु॥
translation: Still do I not hear the inarticulate though sweet and delicious voice of beasts and birds crying in chorus.* *Some text read muhus, momentarily.

sanskrit: चन्दनागुरुसम्पृक्तो धूपसम्मूर्छितोऽमलः। प्रवाति पवनः श्रीमान् किं नु नाद्य यथा पुरा ॥
translation: Why, as before, does not the blameless* and bland wind blow mixed with the perfume of sandal and faint with Dhūpa? *Some texts read atula in place of amala, incomparable.

sanskrit: भेरीमृदङ्गवीणानां कोणसंघट्टितः पुनः। किमद्य शब्दो विरतः सदादीनगतिः पुरा॥
translation: And why, again, have the sounds of Vīņās and Mļdangas developed by beating sticks, which continually flew in a never-ceasing vigorous courses, ceased to-day?

sanskrit: अनिष्टानि च पापानि पश्यामि विविधानि च। निमित्तान्यमनोज्ञानि तेन सीदति मे मनः॥
translation: I witness various evil, unsightly, and unpleasant* omens, and hence my mind is depressed. *The commentator renders amongnani, inauspicious. I venture to differ from him.,

sanskrit: सर्वथा कुशलं सूत दुर्लभं मम बन्धुषु। तथा ह्यसति सम्मोहे हृदयं सीदतीव मे॥
translation: O charioteer, complete good fortune with my friends is hardly to be realised. But although no apparent cause exists for my depression of spirits, yet my heart droopeth.

sanskrit: विषण्णः श्रान्तहृदयस्त्रस्तः संलुलितेन्द्रियः। भरतः प्रविवेशाशु पुरीमिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्॥
translation: Then Bharata depressed and cast down and with his senses afflicted, speedily entered the city ruled by Ikşvāku.

sanskrit: द्वारेण वैजयन्तेन प्राविशच्छ्रान्तवाहनः। द्वा:स्थैरुत्थाय विजयं पृष्ठस्तैः सहितो ययौ॥
translation: And Bharata having his vehicles fatigued, entered by the Vaijayanta* gate, and went on, followed by the gate-keepers, who enquired after his welfare. *Vijayantena. Another meaning is, By the gate resembling that of Indra's palace.

sanskrit: स त्वनेकाग्रहृदयो द्वा:स्थं प्रत्यर्च्य तं जनम्। सूतमश्वपतेः क्लान्तमब्रवीत् तत्र राघवः॥ किमहं त्वरयानीत: कारणेन विनानघ। अशुभाशङ्कि हृदयं शीलं च पततीव मे॥
translation: Then courteously telling the warders to desist, he with an agitated heart spoke to the tired charioteer of Aśvapati, “O sinless one, why have I been brought in this haste without any (adequate) reason?" My heart apprehended some evil; and my disposition gives way.

sanskrit: श्रुता नु यादृशाः पूर्वं नृपतीनां विनाशने। आकारांस्तानहं सर्वानिह पश्यामि सारथे॥
translation: O charioteer, I see around me all those signs which I had heard told as occurring on the occasion of he death of monarchs.

sanskrit: सम्मार्जनविहीनानि परुषाण्युपलक्षये। असंयतकवाटानि श्रीविहीनानि सर्वशः॥ बलिकर्मविहीनानि धूपसम्मोदनेन च। अनाशितकुटुम्बानि प्रभाहीनजनानि च॥ अलक्ष्मीकानि पश्यामि कुटिम्बिभवनान्यहम्। अपेतमाल्यशोभानि असम्मृष्टाजिराणि च॥ देवागाराणि शून्यानि न भान्तीह यथा पुरा।
translation: I behold the houses of the citizens unswept and unsightly with the doors flung open, and destitute of grace, without sacrifices and other religious ceremonies, without the incense of Dhūpa, the citizens fasting, and the people appearing with faded countenance, displaying no flags, etc., The abodes of the deities are not decorated with garlands, and their courts are unclean; and remaining vacant, they look. no longer beautiful as formerly.

sanskrit: देवताः प्रविद्धाश्च यज्ञगोष्ठास्तथैव च॥ माल्यापणेषु राजन्ते नाद्य पण्यानि वा तथा। दृश्यन्ते वणिजोऽप्यद्य न यथापूर्वमत्र वै॥ ध्यानसंविग्नहदया नष्टव्यापारयन्त्रिताः।
translation: The images are not worshipped; and the places of sacrifice are in a like condition. And garlands are not displayed in the shops where they are sold. And traders looking anxious, with their business stopped, do not look as before.

sanskrit: देवायतनचैत्येषु दीनाः पक्षिगास्तथा॥ मलिनं चाश्रुपूर्णाक्षं दीनं ध्यानपरं कृशम्। सस्त्र.पुरां च पश्याम जनमुत्कण्ठितं पुरे॥
translation: And in temples and Caityas birds and beasts appear dispirited. And in the city I behold men and women pale and woe-begone and emaciated and anxious, with tears filling their eyes.

sanskrit: इत्येवमुक्त्वा भरतः सूतं तं दीनमानसः। तान्यनिष्टान्ययोध्यायां प्रेक्ष्य राजगृहं ययौ॥
translation: Having said this to the charioteer, Bharata, beholding these inauspicious sights, entered the palace of the king with a depressed heart.

sanskrit: तां शून्यशृङ्गाटकवेश्मरथ्यां रजोरुणद्वारकवाटयन्त्राम्। दृष्ट्वा पुरीमिन्द्रपुरीप्रकाशां दुःखेन सम्पूर्णतरो बभूव॥
translation: Beholding the city resembling the city of Indra, with her crossings and houses and roads void of people, and the doors and hinges covered with dust, Bharata was filled with greater grief.

sanskrit: बभूव पश्यन्मनसोऽप्रियाणि यान्यन्यदा नास्य पुरे बभूवुः। अवाक्शिरा दीनमना न हृष्टः पितुर्महात्मा प्रविवेश वेश्म ॥
translation: And witnessing many unpleasant things which he had never seen during the life of the monarch, that high-souled one entered the mansion of his father, bending his head, depressed in spirits, and with his mind extremely aggrieved.

sanskrit: अपश्यंस्तु ततस्तत्र पितरं पितुरालये। जगाम भरतो द्रष्टुं मातरं मातुरालये॥
translation: Not having seen his father in his father's quarters, Bharata went to his mother's apartment for seeing her. *The text is evidently corrupt. From the sequel it appears that Bharata has not seen the king at that time. That commentator, however, passes over the point in silence, which is to be accounted for by the slovenliness of the way of though characterising the Sanskrit commentators in general. An English commentator would have considered the matter as of very great importance, but his Hindu brother takes it quietly, and passes on with indifference.

sanskrit: अनुप्राप्तं तु तं दृष्ट्वा कैकेयी प्रोषितं सुतम्। उत्पपात तदा हृष्टा त्यक्त्वा सौवर्णमासनम्॥
translation: On seeing her son before her after his sojourn from home, Kaikeyi delighted, rose up from her golden seat.

sanskrit: स प्रविश्यैव धर्मात्मा स्वगृहं श्रीविवर्जितम्। भरतः प्रेक्ष्य जग्राह जनन्याश्चरणौ शुभौ॥
translation: On entering his own quarter which he found deprived of grace, the virtuous Bharata took hold of his mother's auspicious feet.

sanskrit: तं मूर्ध्नि समुपाघ्राय परिष्वज्य यशस्विनम्। अङ्के भरतमारोप्य प्रष्टुं समुपक्रमे॥
translation: Then smelling the crown of his head and embracing him and taking that illustrious one on her lap, Kaikeyi addressed him, saying.

sanskrit: अद्य ते कतिचिद् रात्र्यश्च्युतस्यार्यकवेश्मनः। अपि नाध्वश्रमः शीघ्रं रथेनापततस्तव॥
translation: How many days hence did you leave the residence of the revered one? Have you felt any fatigue on the way incident to the car proceeding swiftly?

sanskrit: आर्यकस्ते सुकुशली युधाजिन्मातुलस्तव। प्रवासाच्च सुखं पुत्र सर्वं मे वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
translation: And is the revered one will, and your maternal uncle, Yuddhajit? And, my son, have you passed your time pleasantly during your sojourn? It behoves you to tell me all this.

sanskrit: एवं पृष्ठस्तु कैकेय्या प्रियं पार्थिवनन्दनः। आचष्ट भरतः सर्व मात्र राजीवलोचनः।७।।
translation: Thus asked that son of the king, Bharata, furnished with eyes resembling lotuses, told his mother that all was well.

sanskrit: अद्य मे सप्तमी रात्रिश्च्युतस्याकवेश्मनः। अम्बायाः कुशली तातो युधाजिन्मातुलश्च मे॥
translation: Seven nights hence I took leave of that revered one's residence. My mother's sire is well, as also my maternal uncle, Yuddhajit.

sanskrit: यन्मे धनं च रत्नं च ददौ राजा परंतपः। परिश्रान्तं पथ्यभवत् ततोऽहं पूर्वमागतः॥ राजवाक्यहरैर्दूतैस्त्वर्यमाणोऽहमागतः। यदहं प्रष्टुमिच्छामि तदम्बा वक्तुमर्हति ॥
translation: My vehicles had got tired in consequence of bearing the wealth and jewels which that subduer of foes, the king, had bestowed on me. And it is for this reason that I have come in advance of them. Urged by the royal emissaries, I have come here so swiftly. But it behoves my mother to tell me what I wish to ask.

sanskrit: शून्योऽयं शयनीयस्ते पर्यङ्को हेमभूषितः। न चायमिक्ष्वाकुजनः प्रहृष्टः प्रतिभाति मे॥
translation: This sleeping bedstead of yours adorned with gold is empty. I do not see the race of Ikşvāku in their usual good spirits.

sanskrit: राजा भवति भूयिष्ठमिहाम्बाया निवेशने। तमहं नाद्य पश्यामि द्रष्टुमिच्छनिहागतः॥
translation: The king generally remains in this apartment of my mother. But coming here with the desire of seeing him, I do not today find him at this place.

sanskrit: पितुर्ग्रहीष्ये पादौ च तं ममाख्याहि पृच्छतः। आहोस्विदम्बाज्येष्ठायाः कौसल्याया निवेशने॥
translation: I would take the feet of my father. Do you tell me who ask you. Is he in the apartment of my eldest mother, Kausalya?

sanskrit: तं प्रत्युवाच कैकेयी प्रियवद् घोरमप्रियम्। अजानन्तं प्रजानन्ती राज्यलोभेन मोहिता॥
translation: Blinded by the lust of dominion, and looking upon that as desirable (to Bharata) which was exceedingly disagreeable (to him), Kaikeyi replied to him, who did not know what had transpired.

sanskrit: या गतिः सर्वभूतानां तां गतिं ते पिता गतः। राजा महात्मा तेजस्वी यायजूकः सतां गतिः॥
translation: That high-souled and energetic one ever engaged in sacrifice, the refuge of the good, your father, the king, has come by the state which pertains to all creatures.

sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतो वाक्यं धर्माभिजनवाञ्छुचिः। पपात सहसा भूमौ पितृशोकबलार्दितः॥ हा हतोऽस्मीति कृपणां दीनां वाचमुदीरयन्। निपपात महाबाहुर्बाहू विक्षिप्य वीर्यवान्॥
translation: Hearing these words, Bharata of pure ways sprung from a righteous race, smite with the vehemence of sorrow on account of his father, suddenly fell down to the earth. And exclaiming in the anguish of spirit and in the excess of grief, the words, "Ah me! I am undone!" that mightyarmed one endowed with prowess, fell down, tossing about his arms.

sanskrit: ततः शोकेन संवीतः पितुर्मरणदुःखितः। विललाप महातेजा भ्रान्ताकुलितचेतनः॥
translation: Then, overwhelmed with and distressed at the death of his father, that highly sorrow energetic one, with his senses distracted, indulged in lamentations.

sanskrit: एतत् सुरुचिरं भाति पितुर्मे शयनं पुरा। शशिनेवामलं रात्रौ गगनं तोयदात्यये॥ तदिदं न विभात्यद्य विहीनं तेन धीमता। व्योमेव शशिना हीनमप्शुष्क इव सागरः॥
translation: This bed of my father used to look like the speckless welkin at night crowned with the moon, after the clouds have gone off. But to-day, deprived of that intellignet one, it ceases to shine, like the firmament without the moon or the sea devoid of its waters.

sanskrit: बाष्पमुत्सृज्य कण्ठेन स्वात्मना परिपीडितः। प्रच्छाद्य वदनं श्रीमद् वस्त्रेण जयतां वरः॥
translation: Exclaiming with tears trickling down, that foremost of victorious ones, extremely afflicted at heart, wept, muffling his graceful countenance.

sanskrit: तमार्तं देवसंकाशं समीक्ष्य पतितं भुवि। निकृत्तमिव सालस्य स्कन्धं परशुना वने॥ माता मातङ्गसंकाशं चन्दार्कसदृशं सुतम्। उत्थापयित्वा शोकार्तं वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Seeing that one resembling a celestial fallen to the earth, stricken with sorrow, like to a bough of the Sāla that had been severed in the wood by an axe, his mother raising up he distressed son like a mad elephant or the sun or the moon, addressed him.

sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ किं शेषे राजन्नत्र महायशः। त्वद्विधा नहि शोचन्ति सन्तः सदसि सम्मताः॥
translation: Arise, arise. Why do you lie down, O illustrious son of the king? Persons like you having their senses under perfect control, and approved by men of culture, do not grieve.

sanskrit: दानयज्ञाधिकारा हि शीलश्रुतितपोनुगा। बुद्धिस्ते बुद्धिसम्पन्न प्रभेवार्कस्य मन्दिरे॥
translation: O you endo!. ed with understanding, like the halo of the Sun in the solar disc, your sense, entitled to dispensing gifts and celebrating sacrifices, ever follows morals your Śruti and asceticism.

sanskrit: स रुदित्वा चिरं कालं भूमौ परिविवृत्य च। जननी प्रत्युवाचेदं शोकैर्बहुभिरावृतः॥
translation: Having wept for a long while with his body rolling on the earth, Bharata afflicted with manifold grief, answered his mother, saying.

sanskrit: अभिषेक्ष्यति रामं तु राजा यज्ञं नु यक्ष्यते। इत्यहं कृतसंकल्पो हृष्टो यात्रामयासिषम्॥
translation: The king will install Rāma and celebrate a sacrifice' concluding this for certain, I had joyfully gone from hence.

sanskrit: तदिदं ह्यन्यथाभूतं व्यवदीर्णं मनो मम। पितरं यो न पश्यामि नित्यं प्रियहिते रतम्॥
translation: But it has fallen out otherwise. That I do not behold my father ever engaged in the dear welfare (of his subjects) cleaves my heart mother.

sanskrit: अम्ब केनात्यगाद् राजा व्याधिना मय्यनागते। धन्या रामादयः सर्वे यैः पिता संस्कृतः स्वयम्॥
translation: Of what ailment has the king breathed his last during my absence? Blessed are Rāma and others who have personally performed my sire's last rites.

sanskrit: न नूनं मां महाराजः प्राप्तं जानाति कीर्तिमान्। उपजिभ्रेत् तु मां मूर्ध्नि तात: संनाम्य सत्वरम्॥
translation: Surely the renowned monarch does not know that I have come. (If he had done so), pressing down my head, my father would at once have smelt it.

sanskrit: क्व स पाणिः सुखस्पर्शस्तातस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। यो हि मां रजसा ध्वस्तमभीक्ष्णं परिमार्जति॥
translation: Where is now the soft hand of that energetic one which used to rub my person when it was covered with dust?

sanskrit: यो मे भ्राता पिता बन्धुर्यस्य दासोऽस्मि सम्मतः। तस्य मां शीघ्रमाख्याहि रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः॥
translation: Do you now without delay convey the news of my arrival to the vigorous Rāma, who is at once my father, brother and friend, and whose beloved servant I am.

sanskrit: पिता हि भवति ज्येष्ठो धर्ममार्यस्य जानतः। तस्य पादौ ग्रहीष्यामि स हीदानी गतिर्मम ॥
translation: The eldest brother of one that is noble and cognisant of morality, becomes his father. I shall take hold of his feet: he is now my refuge.

sanskrit: धर्मविद् धर्मशीलश्च महाभागो दृढव्रतः। आर्ये किमब्रवीद् राजा पिता मे सत्यविक्रमः॥ पश्चिमं साधुसंदेशमिच्छामि श्रोतुमात्मनः।
translation: And, O noble lady, what did that virtuous one cognizant of virtue, that pre-eminently pious one, firm in his vow, and having truth for prowess, even my father, say? I wish to hear news concerning us relative to the last moments of the monarch.

sanskrit: इति पृष्टा यथातत्त्वं कैकेयी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ रामेति राजा विलपन् हा सीते लक्ष्मणेति च। स महात्मा परं लोकं गतो मतिमतां वरः॥ इतीमा पश्चिमां वाचं व्याजहार पिता तव। कालधर्म परिक्षिप्तः पाशैरिव महागजः॥
translation: Thus asked, Kaikeyi related all as it had happened, saying, “Bewailing 'Ah Rama!' 'Ah Sita!' “Ah Laksmana!' that magnanimous one, the foremost of those that have attained to excellent state (after death), has gone to the next world coming under the law of time.

sanskrit: सिद्धार्थास्तु नरा राममागतं सह सीतया। लक्ष्मणं च महाबाहुं द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुनरागतम्॥
translation: Your father like a mighty elephant fast bound with a cord, said to me these words during his last moments, "Blessed are they that shall see Rāma and the mighty-armed Lakşmaņa returned along with Sītā.”

sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा विषसादैव द्वितीयाप्रियशंसनात्। विषण्णवदनो भूत्वा भूयः पप्रच्छ मातरम्॥
translation: Hearing this, Bharata apprehending a second misfortune was deeply moved; and with a sad countenance, he again asked his mother.

sanskrit: क्व चेदानीं च धर्मात्मा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्राता सीतया च समागतः॥
translation: Where has gone that righteous-souled one, the enchancer of Kausalya's joy, along with Laks maņa and Sītā?

sanskrit: तथा पृष्टा यथान्यायमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे। मातास्य युगपद्वाक्यं विप्रियं प्रियशंसया॥
translation: Thus questioned, his mother at the same time duly said in words which although highly unwelcome, she took as agreeable to Bharata.

sanskrit: स हि राजसुतः पुत्र चीरवासा महावनम्। दण्डकान् सह वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणानुचरो गतः॥
translation: O son, that son of the king wearing bark has repaired to the forest of Dandaka, along with Vaidehi and followed by Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतस्त्रस्तो भ्रातुश्चारित्रशङ्कया। स्वस्य वंशस्य माहात्म्यात् प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे॥
translation: Hearing this, Bharata apprehending some moral lapse on the part of his brother from the dignity of his race, asked in agitation.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्न ब्राह्मणधनं हृतं रामेण कस्यचित्। कच्चिन्नाढ्यो दरिद्रो वा तेनापापो विहिंसितः॥
translation: Has Rāma deprived any Brāhmaṇa of his wealth? Or has he wronged any innocent person, whether rich or poor?

sanskrit: कच्चिन्न परदारान् वा राजपुत्रोऽभिमन्यते। कस्मात् स दण्डकारण्ये भ्राता रामो विवासितः॥
translation: Has the fancy of the prince gone after the wife of another? For what reason has brother Rāma been banished?

sanskrit: अथास्य चपला माता तत् स्वकर्म यथातथम्। तेनैव स्त्रीस्वभावेन व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे॥
translation: Thereat his volatile mother, influenced by her feminine nature, related faithfully to him her own doings.

sanskrit: एवमुक्ता तु कैकेयी भरतेन महात्मना। उवाच वचनं हृष्टा वृथापण्डितमानिनी॥
translation: Thus asked by the magnanimous Bharata, Kaikeyi vainly pluming herself on her wisdom, joyfully said.

sanskrit: न ब्राह्मणधनं किंचिद्धृतं रामेण कस्यचित्। कश्चिन्नाढ्यो दरिद्रो वा तेनापापो विहिंसितः। न रामः परदारान् स चक्षुामपि पश्यति॥
translation: Rāma has deprived no Brāhmaṇa of his property, nor has any innocent person rich or otherwise been wronged by him, nor does he ever with his eyes look at the wife of another.

sanskrit: मया तु पुत्र श्रुत्वैव रामस्येहाभिषेचनम्। याचितस्ते पिता राज्यं रामस्य च विवासनम्॥
translation: O son, as soon as I heard of Råma's (coming) installation, I asked for the kingdom to be conferred on you, and Rāma to be banished.

sanskrit: स स्ववृत्तिं समास्थाय पिता ते तत् तथाकरोत्। रामस्तु सहसौमित्रिः प्रेषितः सह सीतया॥ तमपश्यन् प्रियं पुत्रं महीपालो महायशाः। पुत्रशोकपरिवूनः पञ्चत्वमुपपेदिवान्॥
translation: Thereupon, he, staying by his promise, did accordingly: Rāma has been banished along with Sumitrā's son and Sītā. Not seeing his beloved son, the illustrious lord of earth, stricken by grief on his account, has breathed his last.

sanskrit: त्वया त्विदानी धर्मज्ञ राजत्वमवलम्ब्यताम्। त्वत्कृते हि मया सर्वमिदमेवंविधं कृतम्॥
translation: Do you now, O you cognizant of duty, take charge of the kingdom. I have done all this in your interests.

sanskrit: मा शोकं मा च संतापं धैर्यमाश्रय पुत्रक। त्वदधीना हि नगरी राज्यं चैतदनामयम्॥
translation: Do not give way to sorrow. O son, assume patience. This city is subject to you, as well as this peaceful kingdom.

sanskrit: वसिष्ठमुख्यैः सहितो द्विजेन्द्रैः। मात्मानमुक्मभिषेचयस्व॥
translation: Having with the help of the principal Brāhmaṇas headed by Vasiştha, duly performed the funeral obsequies of the king, do you, without suffering your energy to depart, install yourself in the kingdom.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा च स पितुर्वत्तं भ्रातरौ च विवासितौ। भरतो दुःखसंतप्त इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Hearing of his father's death and the exile of his brothers, Bharata burning in grief, said these words.

sanskrit: किं नु कार्यं हतस्येह मम राज्येन शोचतः। विहीनस्याथ पित्रा च भ्रात्रा पितृसमेन च॥
translation: Deprived of my father as well as my brother like to a father, what shall I bewailing them and undone by you do with the kingdom?

sanskrit: दुःखे मे दुःखमकरोत्रणे क्षारमिवाददाः। राजानं प्रेतभावस्थं कृत्वा रामं च तापसम्॥
translation: You, like one throwing alkali on a sore, have, by bringing about the death of the king and making Rāma an ascetic, heaped grief on grief.

sanskrit: कुलस्य त्वमभावाय कालरात्रिरिवागता। अङ्गारमुपगूह्य स्म पिता मे नावबुद्धवान् ॥
translation: You have come like the fatal night for the destruction of this race. Not under-standing it, my father embraced live coal.

sanskrit: मृत्युमापादितो राजा त्वया मे पापदर्शिनि। सुखं परिहतं मोहाद् कुलेऽस्मिन् कुलपांसनि ॥
translation: O you that have your gaze fixed on sin, it is through you that my sovereign has come by death; and that, O stainer of the line, this race has by your infatuation been deprived of its happiness.

sanskrit: त्वां प्राप्य हि पिता मेऽद्य सत्यसंधो महायशाः। तीव्रदुःखाभिसंतप्तो वृत्तो दशरथो नृपः॥
translation: Having got you, my illustrious sire intent upon truth, king Dasaratha, afflicted by extreme sorrow, has departed this life.

sanskrit: विनाशितो महाराजः पिता मे धर्मवत्सलः। कस्मात् प्रवाजितो रामः कस्मादेव वनं गतः॥
translation: Why has the king, my father, ever loving virtue, been deprived of life? Why has Rāma been banished; and wherefore has he gone to the woods?

sanskrit: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च पुत्रशोकाभिपीडिते। . दुष्करं यदि जीवेतां प्राप्य त्वां जननी मम॥
translation: Afflicted with grief for their son, even if Kausalya and Sumitrā live, it will be hard for them to do so in the presence of you, my mother.

sanskrit: नन्वार्योऽपि च धर्मात्मात्वयि वृत्तिमनुत्तमाम्। वर्तते गुरुवृत्तिज्ञो यथा मातरि वर्तते॥
translation: Surely the noble and virtuous Råma, well knowing his duties towards his superiors, regards you as highly as he does his own mother.

sanskrit: तथा ज्येष्ठा हि मे माता कौसल्या दीर्घदर्शिनी। त्वयि धर्म समास्थाय भगिन्यामिव वर्तते॥
translation: In the same way, my eldest mother, the farsighted Kausalyā, doing her duties by you, bears herself like a sister.

sanskrit: तस्याः पुत्रं महात्मानं चीरवल्कलवाससम्। प्रस्थाप्य वनवासाय कथं पापे न शोचसे॥
translation: Why, O sinful one, having sent to the woods her magnanimous son, clad in bark, do you not grieve?

sanskrit: अपापदर्शिनं शूरं कृतात्मानं यशस्विनम्। प्रव्राज्य चीरवसनं किं नु पश्यसि कारणम्॥
translation: Having exiled the famous and heroic Rāma seeing no sin, clad in bark, what benefit do you perceive as yours?

sanskrit: लुब्धाया विदिती मन्ये न तेऽहं राघवं यथा। तथा ह्यनर्थो राज्यार्थं त्वयानीतो महानयम्॥
translation: I deem that you did not know how very highly I regarded Rāghava; and therefore it is that you have brought this mighty calamity.

sanskrit: अहं हि पुरुषव्याघ्रावपश्यन् रामलक्ष्मणौ। केन शक्तिप्रभावेण राज्यं रक्षितुमुत्सहे॥
translation: Not seeing those chiefs of men, Rāma and Lakşmaņa, by virtue of whose energy can I venture to rule the kingdom?

sanskrit: तं हि नित्यं महाराजो बलवन्तं महौजसम्। उपाश्रितोऽभूद् धर्मात्मा मेरुमैरुवनं यथा ॥
translation: The monarch was ever protected by that powerful one possessed of mighty energy, as Meru is protected by its forest.

sanskrit: सोऽहं कथमिमं भारं महाधुर्यसमुद्यतम्। दम्यो धुरमिवासाद्य सहेयं केन चौजसा ॥
translation: Like a calf burdened with a load capable of being borne by a mighty ox, by what energy shall I bear this burden which was borne by an exceedingly strong person?

sanskrit: अथवा मे भवेच्छक्तिर्योगैर्बुद्धिबलेन वा। सकामां न करिष्यामि त्वामहं पुत्रगर्धिनीम्॥
translation: And even if this strength be mine through yoga or vigour of intellect, I will not crown with success the hopes of you, proud of your son.

sanskrit: न मे विकाङ्क्षा जायेत त्यक्तुं त्वां पापनिश्चयाम्। यदि रामस्य नावेक्षा त्वयि स्यान्मातृवत् सदा॥
translation: Nor, had Rāma not always regarded you as his mother, would I hesitate to renounce you, whose heart has been set on sin.

sanskrit: उत्पन्ना तु कथं बुद्धिस्तवेयं पापदर्शिनी। साधुचारित्रविभ्रष्टे पूर्वेषां नो विगर्हिता॥
translation: O you that views unrighteousness, O you that have fallen off from the way of the good, how could such thoughts unworthy of our line, arise in your mind?

sanskrit: अस्मिन् कुले हि सर्वेषां ज्येष्ठो राज्येऽभिषिच्यते। अपरे भ्रातरस्तस्मिन् प्रवर्तन्ते समाहिताः॥
translation: In this race, the eldest brother of al} is installed in the kingdom: the other brothers remain under him.

sanskrit: न हि मन्ये नृशंसे त्वं राजधर्ममवेक्षसे। गतिं वा न विजानासि राजवृत्तस्य शाश्वतीम्॥
translation: O fell one, you did not, I think, know the morality of kings, or the consequence that attends its faithful observance.

sanskrit: सततं राजपुत्रेषु ज्येष्ठो राजाभिषिच्यते। राज्ञामेतत् समं तत् स्यादिक्ष्वाकूणां विशेषतः॥
translation: Of all the princes, the eldest is always installed as the king. Even this is the accepted principle of all sovereigns, specially the descendants of Ikşvāku.

sanskrit: तेषां धर्मैकरक्षाणां कुलचारित्रशोभिनाम्। अद्य चारित्रशौटीर्यं त्वां प्राप्य विनिवर्तितम्॥
translation: But to-day the pride of character of those whose virtue was their sole concern,* and who shone in the character of their line, has been humbled through they instrumentality. *Another interpretation is;, Whose virtue is their sole protector.

sanskrit: तवापि सुमहाभागे जनेन्द्रकुलपूर्वके। बुद्धिमोहः कथमयं सम्भूतस्त्वयि गर्हितः॥
translation: And how, O highly exalted lady, O you that born in a royal race, could such reprehensible fatuity take possession of your senses?

sanskrit: न तु कामं करिष्यामि तवाहं पापनिश्चये। यया व्यसनमारब्धं जीवितान्तकरं मम॥
translation: But, O you bent upon sin, I will by no means fulfil the wish of you by whom has been brought in the first instance this calamity calculated to end my existence.

sanskrit: एष त्विदानीमेवाहमप्रियार्थं तवानघे। निवर्तयिष्यामि वनाद् भ्रातरं स्वजनप्रियम्॥
translation: Further, O sinless one, I will do this at present was to displease you: I will bring from the forest my brother dear to his relatives.

sanskrit: निवर्तयित्वा रामं च तस्याहं दीप्ततेजसः। दासभूतो भविष्यामि सुस्थितेनान्तरात्मना॥
translation: And having brought back Rāma, I will in a perfectly contented spirit, became the slave of that one of flaming energy.

sanskrit: इत्येवमुक्त्वा भरतो महात्मा प्रियेतरैर्वाक्यगणैस्तुदंस्ताम्। शोकार्दितश्चापि ननाद भूयः सिंहो यथा मन्दरकन्दरस्थः॥
translation: The high-souled Bharata afflicted (his mother) with multitudes of words causing pain; and distressed with grief, emitted sounds like to a lion in the cave of Mandāra.

sanskrit: तां तथा गर्हयित्वा तु मातरं भरतस्तदा। रोषेण महताविष्टः पुनरेवाब्रवीद् वचः॥
translation: Having thus reproved his mother in great wrath, Bharata said again.

sanskrit: राज्याद् भ्रंशस्व कैकेयि नृशंसे दुष्टचारिणि। परित्यक्तासि धर्मेण मा मृतं रुदती भव॥
translation: Do you bear yourself from this kingdom, O heartless and wicked Kaikeyī. Having been lost to righteousness, do not you lament me dead.

sanskrit: किं नु तेऽदूषयद् रामो राजा वा भृशधार्मिकः। ययोर्मृत्युर्विवासश्च त्वत्कृते तुल्यमागतौ॥
translation: What qualities of yours were taxed by the king or the exceedingly virtuous Rāma, that both of them simultaneously have come by death and exile respectively through your agency?

sanskrit: भ्रूणहत्यामसि प्राप्ता कुलस्यास्य विनाशनात्। कैकेयी नरकं गच्छ मा च तातसलोकताम्॥
translation: O Kaikeyī, you have been guilty of homicide in consequence of the destruction of this race. Do you go to hell, never to the world attained by my father.

sanskrit: यत्त्वया हीदृशं पापं कृतं घोरेण कर्मणा। सर्वलोकप्रियं हित्वा ममाप्यापादितं भयम्॥
translation: Since, renouncing Rāma dear to all, you have committed this sin by your grim act and brought me into fear.

sanskrit: त्वत्कृते मे पिता वृत्तो रामश्चारण्यमाश्रितः। अयशो जीवलोके च त्वयाहं प्रतिपादितः॥
translation: Through you has my father met with his end, and Rāma has taken refuge in the woods; and it is through you that I have come to ignominy among all creatures.

sanskrit: मातृरूपे ममामित्रे नृशंसे राज्यकामुके। न तेऽहमभिभाष्योऽस्मि दुर्वृत्ते पतिघातिनि।७।।
translation: O you enemy of mine in the guise of a mother! O fell one! O you that covetest the kingdom! do you not speak to me, O wicked wretch!

sanskrit: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च याश्चान्या मम मातरः। दुःखेन महताविष्टास्त्वां प्राप्य कुलदूषिणीम्॥
translation: O slayer of your husband! it is because of you, stainer of your race, that Kausalyā, Sumiträ, and other mothers of mine have been overwhelmed with a mighty sorrow.

sanskrit: न त्वमश्वपतेः कन्या धर्मराजस्य धीमतः। राक्षसी तत्र जातासि कुलप्रध्वंसिनी पितुः॥ यत् त्वया धार्मिको रामो नित्यं सत्यपरायणः। वनं प्रस्थापितो वीरः पितापि त्रिदिवं गतः॥ यत् प्रधानासि तत् पापं मयि पित्रा विना कृते। भ्रातृभ्यां च परित्यक्ते सर्वलोकस्य चाप्रिये॥
translation: You are never the daughter of the pious and intelligent Aśvapati, you are a Rākṣasī born in that race, you that have destroyed my father's race, inasmuch as the virtuous and heroic Rāma ever observing truth has been sent to the woods and my father has ascended heaven through your agency; inasmuch as you that have perpetrated this arch offence, have laid this sin on me, who have been forsaken by my sire, renounced by my brothers, and come by universal disfavour.

sanskrit: कौसल्यां धर्मसंयुक्तां वियुक्तां पापनिश्चये। कृत्वा कं प्राप्स्यसे ह्यद्य लोकं निरयगामिनि॥
translation: O you of sinful ways, having separated the virtuous Kausalya (from her son), what world, O you that repairest to hell, shall be your portion?

sanskrit: किं नावबुध्यसे क्रूरे नियतं बन्धुसंश्रयम्। ज्येष्ठं पितृसमं रामं कौसल्यायात्मसम्भवम्॥
translation: Does you not, O tortuous one, know that that one sprung from Kucalya's, self, my eldest brother Räma, who is like a father to me, has ever been the refuge of his friends?

sanskrit: अङ्गप्रत्यङ्गजः पुत्रो हृदयाच्चाभिजायते। तस्मात् प्रियतरो मातुः प्रिया एव तु बान्धवाः॥
translation: A son born from all the limbs of his mother, comes out from her heart, and therefore it is that he is far dearer to his mother, albeit her friends are dear to her.* *Angapratyangaja: at., born from the limbs principal and minor. The commentator recounts the face, the breast, the abdomen, the hands and the feet as constituting the former; and eyes, fingers, etc., as the latter.

sanskrit: अन्यदा किल धर्मज्ञा सुरभिः सुरसम्मता। वहमानौ ददर्शोर्त्यां पुत्रौ विगतचेतसौ॥
translation: Once on a time, it is related by persons cognizant of morality, Surabhi regarded by the celestials, beheld two of her sons toiling on earth and seeming to be deprived of their senses.

sanskrit: तावर्धदिवसं श्रान्तौ दृष्ट्वा पुत्रौ महीतले। रुरोद पुत्रशोकेन बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणम्॥
translation: And, when the day had been half spent, seeing her sons fatigued on earth, she stricken with grief for them, began to weep with tears flooding her eyes.

sanskrit: अधस्ताद् व्रजतस्तस्याः सुरराज्ञो महात्मनः। बिन्दवः पतिता गात्रे सूक्ष्माः सुरभिगन्धिनः॥
translation: And it came to pass that as the magnanimous sovereign of the celestials was passing below, her fine and fragrant tear drops fell on his person.

sanskrit: निरीक्षमाणस्तां शक्रो ददर्श सुरभिं स्थिताम्। आकाशे विष्टितां दीनां रुदतीं भृशदुःखिताम्॥।
translation: Turning his eyes up, Śakra found Surabhi stationed in the sky, distressed and weeping in extreme anguish of spirit.

sanskrit: तां दृष्ट्वा शोकसंतप्तां वज्रपाणिर्यशस्विनीम्। इन्द्रः प्राञ्जलिरुद्विग्नः सुरराजोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥
translation: Seeing that illustrious one burning in grief, the wielder of the thunder-bolt, Indra the lord of the celestials, waxing anxious, with joined hands said.

sanskrit: भयं कच्चिन्न चास्मासु कुतश्चिद् विद्यते महत्। कुतो निमित्तः शोकस्ते ब्रूहि सर्वहितैषिणि ॥
translation: Is there any great danger in any quarter? Do you, O you that are intent on the welfare of all, say, whence is this grief of yours?

sanskrit: एवमुक्ता तु सुरभिः सुरराजेन धीमता। प्रत्युवाच ततो धीरा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदा॥
translation: Thus addressed by the intelligent king of the celestials, that one well skilled in speech, the sedate Surabhi answered.

sanskrit: शान्तं पापं न वः किंचित् कुतश्चिदमराधिप। अहं तु मग्नौ शौचामि स्वपुत्रौ विषमे स्थितौ॥ एतौ दृष्ट्वा कृशौ दीनौ सूर्यरश्मिप्रतापितौ। बध्यमानौ बलीवौं कर्षकेण दुरात्मना॥
translation: Auspiciousness, O lord of celestials ! No sin is yours. But I mourn my sons fallen into evil plight, having seen them lean, distressed, and burnt by the rays of the sun, Balivardas afflicted by the wicked-minded ploughman.

sanskrit: मम कायात् प्रसूतौ हि दुःखितौ भारपीडितौ। यौ दृष्ट्वा परितप्येऽहं नास्ति पुत्रसमः प्रियः॥
translation: Seeing those that have been born of my body, cast down and in trouble, I grieve: there is none that is dear like to a son.

sanskrit: यस्याः पुत्रसहस्रेस्तु कृत्स्नं व्याप्तमिदं जगत्। तां दृष्ट्वा रुदतीं शक्रो न सुतान् मन्यते परम्॥
translation: Seeing her the whole earth is filled with whose sons by thousands, weeping, Indra understood that none is an object of greater affection than a son.

sanskrit: इन्द्रो ह्यश्रुनिपातं तं स्वगात्रे पुण्यगन्धिनम्। सुरभिं मन्यते दृष्ट्वा भूयसी तामिहेश्वरः॥
translation: And that lord, Indra, also considered Surabhi of a person breathing a sacred odour, whose tears had dropped on his body, as the foremost being on earth.

sanskrit: समाप्रतिमवृत्ताया लोकधारणकाम्यया। श्रीमत्या गुणमुख्यायाः स्वभावपरिचेष्टया॥ यस्याः पुत्रसहस्राणि सापि शोचति कामधुक् । किं पुनर्या विना रामं कौसल्या वर्तयिष्यति॥
translation: Even that one yielding whatever is asked, auspicious, crowned with the choicest virtues,। although having all natural functions, showing equal kindness to all, and of unequalled character, who maintain all creatures, she who has a thousand sons, grieves (for her sons). How can then Kausalyā carry on existence without Rāma?

sanskrit: एकपुत्रा च साध्वी च विवत्सेयं त्वया कृता। तस्मात् त्वं सततं दुःखं प्रेत्य चेह च लप्स्यसे ॥
translation: Chaste and having an only son, that lady has through you been separated from her son, (like a cow separated from her calf). For this, you will always have to suffer misery alike in this world and the next.

sanskrit: अहं त्वपचितिं भ्रातुः पितुश्च सकलामिमाम्। वर्धनं यशसश्चापि करिष्यामि न संशयः॥
translation: I shall for my part completely minister to my brother and father, and shall without doubt, increase my fame.

sanskrit: आनाय्य च महाबाहुं कोसलेन्द्रं महाबलम्। स्वयमेव प्रवेक्ष्यामि वनं मुनिनिषेचितम्॥
translation: Bringing hither the mighty-armed lord of Kosala endowed with immense strength, I myself will repair to the forest inhabited by ascetics.

sanskrit: नाहं पापसंकल्पे पापे पापं त्वया कृतम्। शक्तो धारयितुं पौरैर श्रुकण्ठैर्निरीक्षितः॥
translation: O you that have delivered yourself over to iniquity, I, looked at by the citizens with their throats oppressed with the vapour grief, cannot bear this (burden of) sin heaped on my by you.

sanskrit: सात्वमग्नि प्रविश वा स्वयं वा विश दण्डकान्। रज्जु बद्ध्वाथवा कण्ठे नहि तेऽन्यत् परायणम्॥
translation: Do you enter fire, or dive into Dandaka, or wound a cord round your neck: other desirable way there is none for you.

sanskrit: अहमप्यवनों प्राप्ते रामे सत्यपराक्रमे। कृतकृत्यो भविष्यामि विप्रवासितकल्मषः॥
translation: On Rāma having truth for prowess, obtaining the earth, I, my disgrace removed, shall be blest.

sanskrit: इति नाग इवारण्ये तोमराङ्कुशतोदितः। पपात भुवि संक्रुद्धो निःश्वसन्निव पन्नगः॥
translation: Grieving thus, Bharata, like an elephant in the forest afflicted with a tomara or ankusa,* fell to the earth sighing like an enraged snake. *Names of instruments.

sanskrit: संरक्तनेत्रः शिथिलाम्बरस्तथा विधूतसर्वाभरणः परंतपः। बभूव भूमौ पतितो नृपात्मजः। शचीपतेः केतुरिवोत्सवक्षये॥
translation: With his eyes reddened, and his cloth falling off, and his ornaments cast away, that subduer of foes, the king's son fallen on the earth, resembled a banner of Sakra after the festival is over.

sanskrit: दीर्घकालात् समुत्थाय संज्ञां लब्ध्वा स वीर्यवान्। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां दीनामुद्वीक्ष्य मातरम्॥ सोऽमात्यमध्ये भरतो जननीमभ्यकुत्सयत्। राज्यं न कामये जातु मन्त्रये नापि मातरम्॥ अभिषेकं न जानामि योऽभूद् राज्ञा समीक्षितः। विप्रकृष्टे ह्यहं देशे शत्रुघ्नसहितोऽभवम्॥
translation: Arising after a long while he had regained his consciousness, Bharata endowed with prowess, regarding his distressed mother with eyes filled with tears, began to tax her in the midst of the courtiers: “I had never desired the kingdom. I had never consulted my mother. Nor did I know the installation that had been thought of by the monarch. I was then living in a far country in company with Satrughna."

sanskrit: वनवासं न जानामि रामस्याहं महात्मनः। विवासनं च सौमित्रेः सीतायाश्च यथाभवत्॥
translation: I did not know the banishment of the magnanimous Rāma to the woods, or the exile of Sumitra's son; nor did I know how Sītā came to be banished.

sanskrit: तथैव क्रोशतस्तस्य भरतस्य महात्मनः। कौसल्या शब्दमाज्ञाय सुमित्रां चेदमब्रवीत्॥
translation: As the high-souled Bharata was thus wailing, Kausalyā recognizing his voice spoke to Sumitra.

sanskrit: आगतः क्रूरकार्यायाः कैकेय्या भरतः सुतः। तमहं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि भरतं दीर्घदर्शिनम्॥
translation: Come is Bharata, the son of that one of crooked ways. I am desirous of seeing the farsighted Bharata.

sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा सुमित्रां तां विवर्णवदना कृशा। प्रतस्थे भरतो यत्र वेपमाना विचेतना॥ स तु राजात्मजश्चापि शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा। प्रतस्थे भरतो येन कौसल्याया निवेशनम्॥
translation: Having said this to Sumitrā, that one emaciated and with a pallid countenance, trembling and almost deprived of sensation, went to where Bharata, was. And it came to pass that the king's son, Bharata, along with Śatrughna had just then by the way that led to the same, been proceeding to Kausalyā's quarter.

sanskrit: ततः शत्रुघ्नभरतौ कौसल्या प्रेक्ष्य दुःखितौ। पर्यष्वजेतां दुःखार्ती पतितां नष्टचेतनाम्॥ रुदन्तौ रुदती दुःखात् समेत्यार्या मनस्विनी। भरतं प्रत्युवाचेदं कौसल्या भृशदुःखिता॥
translation: Then Śatrughna and Bharata seeing the aggrieved Kausalyā, embraced the stricken and fallen lady wellnigh deprived of her senses. Thereupon, weeping from grief, the noble and intelligent Kausalyà exceedingly afflicted, embracing them as they indulged in sorrow, said to Bharata.

sanskrit: इदं ते राज्यकामस्य राज्यं प्राप्तमकण्टकम्। सम्प्राप्तं बत कैकेय्या शीघ्रं क्रूरेण कर्मणा॥
translation: Thus have you, that had desired the kingdom, received it rid of its thorn. Alas! it has been speedily obtained through the crooked act of Kaikeyi.

sanskrit: प्रस्थाप्य चीरवसनं पुत्रं मे वनवासिनम्। कैकेयी के गुणं तत्र पश्यति क्रूरदर्शिनी॥
translation: What is the good that is perceived by Kaikeyi of tortuous sight in sending away my son clad in bark to the woods?

sanskrit: क्षिप्रं मामपि कैकेयी प्रस्थापयितुमर्हति। हिरण्यनाभो यत्रास्ते सुतो मे सुमहायशाः॥
translation: It behoves Kaikeyi to send me also speedily to where is staying my illustrious son furnished with a gold-gleaming navel.

sanskrit: अथवा स्वयमेवाहं सुमित्रानुचरा सुखम्। अग्निहोत्रं पुरस्कृत्य प्रस्थास्ये यत्र राघवः॥
translation: Or first performing the fire-sacrifice, I followed by Sumitrā, will myself happily seek the way by which Rāghava (has gone to the woods).

sanskrit: कामं वा स्वयमेवाद्य तत्र मां नेतुमर्हसि। यत्रासौ पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तप्यते मे सुतस्तपः॥
translation: Or it behoves you to yourself bring me to the place where that foremost of men, my son, is performing austerities.

sanskrit: इदं हि तव विस्तीर्णं धनधान्यसमाचितम्। हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पूर्ण राज्यं निर्यातितं तया॥
translation: This spacious kingdom abounding in corn and wealth, and filled with elephants, horses, and cars, is yours, having been conferred on you (by Kaikeyi).

sanskrit: इत्यादिबहुभिर्वाक्यैः क्रूरैः सम्भर्त्तितोऽनघः। विव्यथे भरतोऽतीव व्रणे तुद्येव सूचिना॥
translation: Thus reproached by many a harsh word, the sinless Bharata felt exceeding pain like to that produced by pricking a sore with a needle.

sanskrit: पपात चरणौ तस्यास्तदा सम्भ्रान्तचेतनः। विलप्य बहुधासंज्ञो लब्धसंज्ञस्तदाभवत्॥ एवं विलपमानां तां प्राञ्जलिर्भरतस्तदा। कौसल्या प्रत्युवाचेदं शोकैर्बहुभिरावृताम् ॥
translation: Exceedingly agitated, he fell at Kausalya's feet, lamenting much, and well nigh deprived of his Bharata then regained his consciousness, and with joined hands answered Kausalya lamenting thus and overcome with excess of sorrow, saying.

sanskrit: आर्ये कस्मादजानन्तं गर्हसे मामकल्मषम्। विपुलां च मम प्रीति स्थितां जानासि राघवे॥
translation: O noble lady, what for do you censure me who am without sin and who know nothing of this? You know that profuse is my delight in Rāghava.

sanskrit: कृतशास्त्रानुगा बुद्धिर्मा भूत् तस्य कदाचन। सत्यसंधः सतां श्रेष्ठो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May the sense of him never follow scripture, that had approved the exile into the woods of that foremost of the good, the noble Rāma intent senses. on truth!

sanskrit: प्रेष्यं पापीयसां यातु सूर्यं च प्रति मेहतु। हन्तु पादेन गाः सुप्ता यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May such a person as had approved the exile to the woods of the noble one undergo servitude at the hands of the sinful, answer the calls of nature facing the Sun, and kick a sleeping cow with his feet!

sanskrit: कारयित्वा महत् कर्म भर्ता भृत्यमनर्थकम्। अधर्मो योऽस्य सोऽस्यास्तु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods come by the sin that is reaped by a master who withholds salary from servants after the ceremony is over!

sanskrit: परिपालयमानस्य राज्ञो भूतानि पुत्रवत्। ततस्तु दुह्यतां पापं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May that one that had approved the exile of the noble Rāma to the woods, be guilty of the sin that is his that injures a sovereign engaged in ruling his subjects like sons!

sanskrit: बलिषड्भागमुद्धत्य नृपस्यारक्षितुः प्रजाः। अधर्मो योऽस्य सोऽस्यास्तु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May the person that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods, reap the sin of his that having taken a sixth pare of their incomes, does not protect his subjects!

sanskrit: संश्रुत्य च तपस्विभ्यः सत्रे वै यज्ञदक्षिणाम्। तां चापलतां पापं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods, come by the demerit that is his that denies Dakșiņās to ascetics in a sacrifice, after having promised them the same!

sanskrit: हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधे युद्धे शस्त्रसमाकुले। मास्म कार्षीत् सतां धर्म यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile into the woods of the noble one, never discharge the duty of the good in the field thronged with elephants and horses and cars, and bristling with arms!

sanskrit: उपदिष्टं सुसूक्ष्मार्थं शास्त्रं यत्नेन धीमता। स नाशयतु दुष्टात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May the wicked wight that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods bring to naught the subtle scriptural knowledge which has been carefully taught him by his intelligent preceptor!

sanskrit: मा च तं व्यूढबाह्वसं चन्द्रभास्करतेजसम्। द्राक्षीद् राज्यस्थमासीनं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May that one that had approved the exile of the noble (Rāma) to the woods never behold the long-armed and broad-shouldered (Rāghava) resembling the Sun and the Moon in energy (on the throne)!

sanskrit: पायसं कृसरं छागं वृथा सोऽश्नातु निघृणः। गुरुंश्चाप्यवजानातु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May that one void of aversion, that had approved of the exile of the noble one to the woods feed on Payasa, Krsara, and goat's flesh, which have not been offered in sacrifice; and may he insult his spiritual precept.

sanskrit: गवां स्पृशतु पादेन गुरून् परिवदेत च। मित्रे दुह्येत सोऽत्यर्थं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: Or! May he that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods touch a cow with his feet, revile his superiors, and injure his friends!

sanskrit: विश्वासात् कथितं किंचित् परिवादं मिथः क्वचित्। विवृणोतु स दुष्टात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May that one of wicked soul that had approved of the exile of the noble one into the woods divulge any defects (of another's character) that have been communicated to him in strict confidence!

sanskrit: अकर्ता चाकृतज्ञश्च त्यक्तश्च निरपत्रपः। लोके भवतु विद्विष्टो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of Rāma to the woods, never repay any good act, be ungrateful, abandoned by all, the object of universal execration.

sanskrit: पुत्रैर्दासैश्च भृत्यैश्च स्वगृहे परिवारितः। स एको मृष्टमश्नातु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved of the exile into the woods of the noble one, eat alone in his home, although surrounded by sons and wives and servitors!

sanskrit: अप्राप्य सदृशान् दाराननपत्यः प्रमीयताम्। अनवाप्य क्रियां धर्त्यां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that haå approved of the exile of the noble one, die without obtaining wives worthy of him, without sons, without any good works performed!

sanskrit: मात्मनः संततिं द्राक्षीत् स्वेषु दारेषु दुःखितः। आयुःसमग्रमप्राप्य यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods, never see his own offspring, and not attaining ripe age, may he mourn his wives!

sanskrit: राजस्त्रीबालवृद्धानां वधे यत् पापमुच्यते। भृत्यत्यागे च यत्पापं तत्पापं प्रतिपद्यताम्॥
translation: And may he come by the sin that is reaped by slaying a king, a woman, a boy, or an old man, or by renouncing those who have claims on his maintenance!

sanskrit: लाक्षया मधुमांसेन लोहेन च विषेण च। सदैव बिभृयाद् भृत्यान् यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods always feed his family with lac, honey, meat, iron, and poison!

sanskrit: संग्रामे समुपोढे च शत्रुपक्षभयंकरे। पलायमानो बध्येत यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May that one that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods, while flying from the engagement while it is waxing furious with the foe, come to be killed !

sanskrit: कपालपाणिः पृथिवीमटतां चीरसंवृतः। भिक्षमाणो यथोन्मत्तो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved of the exile of the noble one into the woods, clad in tatters with a skuil in hand, like a madman range the earth abegging!

sanskrit: मद्यप्रसक्तो भवतु स्त्रीष्वक्षेषु च नित्यशः। कामक्रोधाभिभूतश्च यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods, be always addicted to wine, to women, and to dice; and may he be swayed by lust, anger, etc!

sanskrit: मास्य धर्मे मनो भूयादधर्मं स निषेवताम्। अपात्रवर्षी भवतु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved of the exile of that noble one into the woods, never relish virtue, and go after unrighteousness; and may he shower his wealth on the unworthy!

sanskrit: संचितान्यस्य वित्तानि विविधानि सहस्रशः। दस्युभिर्विप्रलुप्यन्तां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods, have his various accumulated riches by thousand carried off by robbers!

sanskrit: उभे संध्ये शयानस्य यत् पापं परिकल्प्यते। तच्च पापं भवेत् तस्य यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥ यदग्निदायके पापं यत् पापं गुरुतल्पगे। मित्रद्रोहे च यत् पापं तत् पापं प्रतिपद्यताम्॥
translation: May he that had approved of the exile into the woods of that noble one, come by the demerit that is his who sleeps during both the twilight's! May he reap the sin that is reaped by an incendiary or him that Leith with his preceptor's wife; or him that wrongs his friend!

sanskrit: देवतानां पितृणां च मातापित्रोस्तथैव च। मा स्म कार्षीत् स शुश्रूषां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of that noble one into the woods, never serve the gods or the manes of the ancestors or his father and mother!

sanskrit: सतां लोकात् सतां कीर्त्याः सज्जुष्टात् कर्मणस्तथा। भ्रश्यतु क्षिप्रमद्यैव यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: may he that had approved the exile of that noble one into the woods, be speedily shut out from the world of the good, from their fame, and from their acts!

sanskrit: अपास्य मातृशुश्रूषामनर्थे सोऽवतिष्ठताम्। दीर्घबाहुमहावक्षा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of that long armed and broad breasted one, renouncing the ministration of his mother, turn his thoughts to evil!

sanskrit: बहुभृत्यो दरिद्रश्च ज्वररोगसमन्वितः। समायात् सततं क्लेशं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one, becoming improved the exile of the noble one, becoming impoverished yet having to support a large family, and suffering from fever, be always miserable! an

sanskrit: आशामाशंसमानानां दीनानामूलचक्षुषाम्। अर्थिनां वितथां कुर्याद् यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile of that noble one render fruitless the hopes of poor people cherishing them and looking up (wistfully).

sanskrit: मायया रमतां नित्यं पुरुषः पिशुनोऽशुचिः। राज्ञो भीतस्त्वधर्मात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile into the woods of the noble one remaining (always) wicked, cruel and impure, leading unrighteous life and being in (continual) fear of his sovereign, maintain himself by deceit for ever and a day!

sanskrit: ऋतुस्नातां सती भार्यामृतुकालानुरोधिनीम्। अतिवर्तेत दुष्टात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः५२।।
translation: May that wicked person that had approved the exile into the woods of that noble one disregard his chaste wife remaining near, after she has performed her ablutions at the end of her season.

sanskrit: विप्रलुप्तप्रजातस्य दुष्कृतं ब्राह्मणस्य यत्। तदेतत् प्रतिपद्येत यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May his that had approved the banishment into the woods of that noble one be the sin that is incurred by a Brāhmana that has rendered himself sonless.

sanskrit: ब्राह्मणायोद्यतां पूजां विहन्तु कलुषेन्द्रियः। बालवत्सां च गां दोग्धुर्यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May that one of befouled senses that had approved of the exile into the woods of that noble one disturb the worship of Brāhmaṇa and milch a cow that has a calf.

sanskrit: धर्मदारान् परित्यज्य परदारान् निषेवताम्। त्यक्तधर्मरतिर्मूढो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May that foolish person that had approved the exile of that noble one forsaking all pleasure in virtue, seek others wives, renouncing his own wedded with sacred rites!

sanskrit: पानीयदूषके पापं तथैव विषदायके। यत्तदेकः स लभतां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile into the woods of that noble one come by the sin that attaches to a wine biber or one that administers poison to another!

sanskrit: तृषार्तं सति पानीये विप्रलम्भेन योजयन्। यत् पापं लभते तत् स्याद् यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved of the exile into the woods of the noble one bear the sin that is his that serves a thirsty soul with deceit.

sanskrit: भक्त्या विवदमानेषु मार्गमाश्रित्य पश्यतः। तेन पापेन युज्येत यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः॥
translation: May he that had approved the exile into the woods of that noble one reap the demerit of them that from devotion to their respective faiths wrangle from their own points of view, as well as that of them that listen to the disputation!

sanskrit: एवमाश्वासयन्नेव दुःखार्तोऽनुपपात ह। विहीनां पतिपुत्राभ्यां कौसल्या पार्थिवात्मजः॥
translation: Having thus consoled Kausalyā bereft of her son and husband, the prince afflicted with distress fell down.

sanskrit: तदा तं शपथैः कष्टैः शपमानमचेतनम्। भरतं शोकसंतप्तं कौसल्या वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Then Kausalyā addressed the aggrieved Bharaia (well-nigh) deprived of his senses, swearing strong oaths, saying.

sanskrit: मम दुःखमिदं पुत्र भूयः समुपजायते। शपथैः शपमानो हि प्राणानुपरुणत्सि मे॥
translation: O son, it grieves me more that you are afflicting my heart by taking oaths.

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या न चलितो धर्मादात्मा ते सहलक्षणः। वत्स सत्यप्रतिज्ञो हि सतां लोकानवाप्स्यसि ॥ इत्युक्त्वा चाङ्कमानीय भरतं भ्रातृवत्सलम्। परिष्वज्य महाबाहुं रुरोद भृशदुःखिता॥
translation: Lucky it is that graced with auspicious marks, you swerves not from virtue. My child, for this reason you will attain the regions of pious person, drawing into her lap Bharata attached to his brother, and embracing the mighty armed one, gave way to grief.

sanskrit: एवं विलपमानस्य दुःखार्तस्य महात्मनः। मोहाच्च शोकसंरम्भाद् बभूव लुलितं मनः॥
translation: And bewailing thus, the mind of the high souled (Bharata) wrought with sorrow, was overcome with the burden of grief.

sanskrit: लालप्यमानस्य विचेतनस्य प्रणष्टबुद्धेः पतितस्य भूमौ। मुहुर्मुहुनिःश्वसतश्च दीर्घ सा तस्य शोकेन जगाम रात्रिः :॥
translation: And fallen the ground, lamenting, senseless, with his intellect overpowered, and momentarily heaving sighs, Bharata passed away night in grief.

sanskrit: तमेवं शोकसंतप्तं भरतं कैकयीसुतम्। उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठो वसिष्ठः श्रेष्ठवागृषिः॥
translation: As Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi was thus burning in grief, that foremost of those skilled in speech, the saint Vasistha, endowed with excellence of language, said.

sanskrit: अलं शोकेन भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः। प्राप्तकालं नरपतेः कुरु संयानमुत्तमम्॥
translation: Do not weep, good betide you, O illustrious prince. Do you perform the funereal rites of the departed king.

sanskrit: वसिष्ठस्य वचः श्रुत्वा भरतो धरणीं गतः। प्रेतकृत्यानि सर्वाणि कारयामास धर्मवित्॥
translation: Hearing Vasistha's words, Bharata cognisant of duty, bowed down to the ground and despatched the ministers for performing the last rites.

sanskrit: उदधृत्य तैलसंसेकात् स तु भूमौ निवेशितम्। आपीतवर्णवदनं प्रसुप्तमिव भूमिपम्॥ संवेश्य शयने चाग्र्ये नानारत्नपरिष्कृते। ततो दशरथं पुत्रो विललाप सुदुःखितः॥
translation: And raising from under the oil the body of the king with a sallow countenance, and appearing to be asleep. Bharata placed it on the ground upon a couch in front adorned with various gems. Then overwhelmed with grief, Dasaratha's son bewailed him thus.

sanskrit: किं ते व्यवसितं राजन् प्रोषिते मय्यनागते। विवास्य रामं धर्मज्ञं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्॥
translation: O king, what was it that you had intended to do, I absent and away from home, by banishing righteous Rāma and the powerful Lakşmana?

sanskrit: क्व यास्यसे महाराज हित्वेमं दु:खितं जनम्। हीनं पुरुषसिंहेन रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ॥
translation: Whither wend you, O mighty monarch, forsaking these aggrieved people, who have already been deprived of the lion like Rāma energetic in action?

sanskrit: योगक्षेमं तु तेऽव्यग्रं कोऽस्मिन् कल्पयिता पुरे। त्वयि प्रयाते स्वस्तात रामे च वनमाश्रिते॥
translation: O father, you having ascended heaven and Rāma having taken refuge in the woods, who now in this city of yours shall protect what the people possess and secure to them what they have not?

sanskrit: विधवा पृथिवी राजंस्त्वया हीना न राजते। हीनचन्द्रव रजनी नगरी प्रतिभाति माम्॥
translation: Widowed in consequence of losing you, this earth does not look graceful. The city appears to me like the night deprived of the Moon

sanskrit: एवं विलपमानं तं भरतं दीनमानसम्। अब्रवीद् वचनं भूयो वसिष्ठस्तु महामुनिः॥
translation: As Bharata was lamenting thus in dejected mood, the mighty ascetic Vasiştha again addressed him, saying.

sanskrit: प्रेतकार्याणि यान्यस्य कर्तव्यानि विशाम्पतेः। तान्यव्यग्रं महाबाहो क्रियतामविचारितम्॥
translation: O mighty armed one, do you without indulging in any reflections, perform those funeral ceremonies of the monarch which ought to be performed.

sanskrit: तथेति भरतो वाक्यं वसिष्टस्याभिपूज्य तत्। ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यास्त्वरयामास सर्वशः॥
translation: Thereupon honouring his words by saying, "So be it,” he urged speed upon all the Rtvigs, priests, and Acāryas.

sanskrit: ये त्वग्नयो नरेन्द्रस्य अग्न्यगाराद् बहुष्कृताः। ऋत्विग्भिर्याजकैश्चैव ते हूयन्ते यथाविधि॥
translation: And then those that had brought the king's corpse out side from the fire chamber, instructed by the Rtvigs and priests according to the ordinance began to offer oblations into the fire.

sanskrit: शिबिकायामथारोप्य राजानं गतचेतनम्। बाष्पकण्ठा विमनसस्तमूचुः परिचारकाः॥
translation: Next placing the king deprived of life on a car, the servants with their throats oppressed with vapour and with their minds weighed down with dejection carried him.

sanskrit: हिरण्यं च सुवर्णं च वासांसि विविधानि च। प्रकिरन्तो जना मार्गे नृपतेरग्रतो ययुः॥
translation: And scattering gold and silver and various kinds of cloth, on the way people went in front of the king.

sanskrit: चन्दनागुरुनिर्यासान् सरलं पद्मकं तथा। देवदारूणि चाहृत्य क्षेपयन्ति तथापरे॥ गन्धानुच्चावचांश्चान्यांस्तत्र गत्वाथ भूमिपम्। तत्र संवेशयामासुश्चितामध्ये तमृत्विजः॥
translation: Others procuring sandal, aguru and other sarala, padmaka and devadari, cast it (on the earth). And drawing near the king there, Rtvigs laid various other fragrant substances on the funeral pile.

sanskrit: तदा हुताशनं हुत्वा जेपुस्तस्य तदृत्विजः। जगुश्च ते यथाशास्त्रं तत्र सामानि सामगाः॥
translation: Then offering oblations into the fire, the Rtvigs began to recite japa; and as laid down in the scriptures, Sāma-singers chanted Sämans.

sanskrit: शिबिकाभिश्च यानैश्च यथार्ह तस्य योषितः। नगरान्निर्ययुस्तत्र वृद्धैः परिवृतास्तथा॥ प्रसव्यं चापि तं चक्रुर्ऋत्विजोऽग्निचितं नृपम्। स्त्रियश्च शोकसंतप्ता: कौसल्याप्रमुखास्तदा॥
translation: By means of litters and other conveyances, each mounted according to her rank, the wives of the king went out from the city, surrounded by aged men. And Rtvijas went round the corpse on the king who performed many sacrifices leaving it on the left side.

sanskrit: क्रौञ्चीनामिव नारीणां निनादस्तत्र शुश्रुवे। आर्तानां करुणं काले क्रोशन्तीनां सहस्रशः॥
translation: And kindling with grief, the females also headed by Kausalyā (circumambulated the pyre). And then there was heard the wail of women distressed with grief weeping piteously by thousands like to Krauñcis.

sanskrit: ततो रुदन्त्यो विवशा विलप्य च पुनः पुनः। यानेभ्यः सरयूतीरमवतेरुपाङ्गनाः॥
translation: Weeping again and again with their sense lost, the wives of the king alighted from the car on the banks of the Sarayu.

sanskrit: कृत्वोदकं ते भरतेन साधु नृपाङ्गना मन्त्रिपुरोहिताश्च। पुरं प्रविश्याश्रुपरीतनेत्रा भूमौ दशाहं व्यनयन्त दुःखम्॥
translation: Having performed the watery rites, the wives of the monarch as well as the counsellors and priests, in company with Bharata entering the city with tears in their eyes, spent ten days* in mourning lying down on the ground. *The Smrti: lays down twelve days of mourning for kings, and sixteen for Khatriyas. Parasara, however, fixes ten days for Ksatriyas in general.

sanskrit: ततो दशाहेऽतिगते कृतशौचो नृपात्मजः। द्वादशेऽहनि सम्प्राप्ते श्राद्धकर्माण्यकारयत्॥
translation: When the ten days had gone by, the king's son, his uncleanness (consequent on the demise of his father) removed, performed the sraddha on the twelfth day.

sanskrit: ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनं रत्नं ददावन्नं च पुष्कलम्। वासांसि च महार्हाणि रत्नानि विविधानि च। बास्तिकं बहु शुक्लं च गाश्चापि बहुशस्तदा॥ दासीर्दासांश्च यानानि वेश्मानि सुमहान्ति च। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ पुत्रो राज्ञस्तस्यौर्ध्वदेहिकम्॥
translation: On the occasion on the ceremonies for the welfare of the departed Spirit, the son of the king conferred on Brāhmaṇas wealth and gems, and rice in abundance, and herds of goats, and silver in profusion, and countless kine, and maidservants and man-servants, and vehicles and spacious mansions.

sanskrit: ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसे च त्रयोदशे। विललाप महाबाहुर्भरतः शोकमूर्च्छितः॥
translation: And on the thirteenth day, the long armed Bharata, overwhelmed with grief, burst into lamentation.

sanskrit: शब्दापिहितकण्ठश्च शोधनार्थमुपागतः। चितामूले पितुर्वाक्यमिदमाह सुदुःखितः॥ तात यस्मिन् निसृष्टोऽहं त्वया भ्रातरि राघवे। तस्मिन् वनं प्रव्रजिते शून्ये त्यक्तोऽस्म्यहं त्वया॥
translation: And coming to the foot of the funeral pyre for gathering the bones of the departed, he overcome with grief, with his throat obstructed with the sounds of lamentation, said, “my father, on brother Rāma, to whom I had been consigned by you, having gone to the forest, I have been cast by you into vacancy.

sanskrit: यस्या गतिरनाथायाः पुत्रः प्रव्राजितो वनम्। तामम्बां तात कौसल्यां त्यक्त्वात्वं व गतोनृप।७।।
translation: My father, forsaking forlorn mother Kausalya, whose stay her son, had gone to the forest, where have you gone, Oking?

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा भस्मारुणं तच्च दग्धास्थि स्थानमण्डलम्। पितुः शरीरनिर्वाणं निष्टनन् विषसाद ह॥
translation: Seeing the spot where lay the bones of his father mixed with ashes and embers Bharata looking at the place where occurred the dissolution of his father's fame, carried away by emotion, indulged in sorrow.

sanskrit: स तु दृष्ट्वा रुदन् दीनः पपात धरणीतले। उत्थाप्यमानः शक्रस्य यन्त्रध्वज इवोच्छ्रितः॥
translation: And seeing this, he exceedingly distressed, crying fell down to the ground. And raised up (by others) he looked like an uplifted banner of Sakra bound to an engine.

sanskrit: अभिपेतुस्ततः सर्वे तस्यामात्याः शुचिव्रतम्। अन्तकाले निपतितं ययातिमृषयो यथा॥
translation: His counsellors rushed towards that one of pure vows, like the saints making towards Yayati as he was falling on the extinction of his merit.

sanskrit: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि भरतं दृष्ट्वा शोकपरिप्लुतम्। विसंज्ञो न्यपतद् भूमौ भूमिपालमनुस्मरन्॥
translation: Seeing Bharata plunged in grief, Satrughna remembering the king, fell down to the ground deprived of consciousness.

sanskrit: उन्मत्त इव निश्चित्तो विललाप सुदुःखितः। स्मृत्वा पितुर्गुणाङ्गानि तानि तानि तदा तदा॥
translation: And devoid of sense and like a madman, he in grief of heart began to lament remembering all the virtues of his father again and again.

sanskrit: मन्थराप्रभवस्तीव्रः कैकेयीग्राहसंकुलः। वरदानमयोऽक्षोभ्योऽमज्जयच्छोकसागरः॥
translation: This terrible sea of grief owing its origin to Mantharā, containing its ferocious aquatic animal in the shape of Kaikeyī, and incapable of being disturbed in consequence of the bestowal of the boon drowns (us).

sanskrit: सुकुमारं च बालं च सततं लालितं त्वया। क तात भरतं हित्वा विलपन्तं गतो भवान् ॥
translation: O father, where have you gone, leaving the tender and youthful Bharata fondled by you, to lament (your loss).

sanskrit: ननु भोज्येषु पानेषु वस्त्रेष्वाभरणेषु च। प्रवारयति सर्वान् नस्तनः कोऽद्य करिष्यति॥
translation: You did use to confer on us eatables and drinkable and attires and ornaments. Who will now do so?

sanskrit: अवदारणकाले तु पृथिवी नावदीर्यते। विहीना या त्वया राज्ञा धर्मज्ञेन महात्मना ॥
translation: Deprived of you, the high souled king cognisant of duty, the earth albeit her time of riving is come, is not yet riven.

sanskrit: पितरि स्वर्गमापन्ने रामे चारण्यमाश्रिते। किं मे जीवितसामर्थ्य प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्॥
translation: My father having gone to heaven and Rāma having sought the woods, how can I live? I will enter fire.

sanskrit: हीनो भ्रात्रा च पित्रा च शून्यामिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्। अयोध्यां न प्रवेक्ष्यामि प्रवेक्ष्यामि तपोवनम्॥
translation: Bereft of my brother and sire, I will not enter the empty Ayodhyā governed by the Ikşvākus. I will repair to the forest of asceticism.

sanskrit: तपोर्विलपितं श्रुत्वा व्यसनं चाप्यवेक्ष्य तत्। भृशमार्ततरा भूयः सर्व एवानुगामिनः॥
translation: Hearing his lamentations and seeing that disaster, all the followers became all the more distressed.

sanskrit: ततो विषण्णौ श्रान्तौ च शत्रुघ्नभरतावुभौ। धरायां स्म व्यचेष्टेतां भग्नशृङ्गविवर्षभौ॥
translation: Then depressed and exhausted, both Šatrughna and Bharata rolled on the earth like two bulls with their horns fractured,

sanskrit: ततः प्रकृतिमान् वैद्यः पितुरेषां पुरोहितः। वसिष्ठो भरतं वाक्यमुत्थाप्य तमुवाच ह॥
translation: Then the all-knowing priest of their father possessed of sterling worth, Vasistha, raising Bharata, said to him.

sanskrit: त्रयोदशोऽयं दिवसः पितुर्वृत्तस्य ते विभो। सावशेषास्थिनिचये किमिह त्वं विलम्बसे ॥
translation: O Lord this is the thirteenth day since the cremation of your sire. Why did you delay, when you have to collect the bones?

sanskrit: त्रीणि द्वन्द्वानि भूतेषु प्रवृत्तान्यविशेषतः। तेषु चापरिहार्येषु नैवं भवितुमर्हसि॥
translation: Three couples* pertain in especial to all creatures and these being inevitable, you ought not to bear yourself thus. *Hunger and thirst, ignorance and grief, sickness and death.

sanskrit: सुमन्त्रश्चापि शत्रुघ्नमुत्थाप्याभिप्रसाद्य च। श्रावयामास तत्त्वज्ञः सर्वभूतभवाभवौ॥
translation: And Sumantra also versed in the nature of things, raising up Šatrughna and pacifying him, discoursed the birth and heath of all beings.

sanskrit: उत्थितौ तौ नरव्याघ्रौ प्रकाशेते यशस्विनौ। वर्षातपपरिग्लानौ पृथगिन्द्रध्वजाविव ॥
translation: Being raised up, those renowned chiefs of men looked like Indra's banner stained by shine and shower.

sanskrit: अश्रूणि परिमृद्गन्तौ रक्ताक्षौ दीनभाषिणौ। अमात्यास्त्वरयन्ति स्म तनयौ चापराः क्रियाः॥
translation: And as the princes stood there shedding tears, with reddened eyes, and speaking sadly, the courers urged nem on in behalf of the rites that remained.

sanskrit: अथ यात्रां समीहन्तं शत्रुघ्ने लक्ष्मणानुजः। भरतं शोकसंतप्तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
translation: Then ſatrughna, the younger brother of Lakşmaņa spoke to Bharata burning in grief as he was revolving in his mind the (intended) journey (to Rāma).

sanskrit: गतिर्यः सर्वभूतानां दुःखे किं पुनरात्मनः। स रामः सत्त्वसम्पन्नः स्त्रिया प्रव्राजितो वनम् ॥
translation: Need it be said that Rāma is the refuge both of himself and all creatures in trouble? That Rāma possessed of strength has been exiled into the woods by a woman!

sanskrit: बलवान् वीर्यसम्पन्नो लक्ष्मणो नाम योऽप्यसौ। किं न मोचयते रामं कृत्वापि पितृनिग्रहम्॥
translation: And powerful and having prowess, why did not Laksmana deliver Rāma by checking our father?

sanskrit: पूर्वमेव तु विग्राह्यः समवेक्ष्य नयानयौ। उत्पथं यः समारूढो नार्या राजा वशं गतः॥
translation: The king bent upon following an unrighteous course through the influence of a woman, should, the justice or otherwise of the measure being fully weighed, at the very outset have been checked.

sanskrit: इति सम्भाषमाणे तु शत्रुघ्ने लक्ष्मणानुजे। प्रारद्वारेऽभूत् तदा कुब्जा सर्वाभरणभूषिता॥ लिप्ता चन्दनसारेण राजवस्त्राणि बिभ्रती। विविधं विविधैस्तैस्तैर्भूषणैश्च विभूषिता॥
translation: As Lakşmaņa's younger brother Satrughna was speaking thus, appeared there at the door in front the hump backed one adorned with every kind of ornament, with her body besmeared with sandal paste, wearing regal apparel, and variously decked out with a variety of ornaments.

sanskrit: मेखलादामभिश्चित्रैरन्यैश्च वरभूषणैः। बभासे बहुभिर्बद्धा रज्जुभिरिव वानरी॥
translation: And adorned with elegant zones, and divers other superb ornaments, she looked like a female monkey tethered with a rope.

sanskrit: तां समीक्ष्य तदा द्वा:स्थो भृशं पापस्य कारिणीम्। गृहीत्वाकरुणं कुब्जां शत्रुघ्नाय न्यवेदयत्॥
translation: At that time seeing that one of horrible misdeeds, (Bharata) who stood near the door, seizing the hump backed one ruthlessly, took her to Satrughna, and said.

sanskrit: यस्याः कृते वने रामो न्यस्तदेहश्च वः पिता। सेयं पापा नृशंसा च तस्याः कुरु यथामति।।।।
translation: That one through whom Rāma has gone to the wood and our father has renounced his body this is that wicked and remorseless one. Do you deal with her as you like.

sanskrit: शत्रुघ्नश्च तदाज्ञाय वचनं भृशदुःखितः। अन्तःपुरचरान् सर्वानित्युवाच धृतव्रतः॥
translation: At Bharata's command Satrughna observing vows waxing exceedingly aggrieved, addressed all the inmates of the inner apartment, saying.

sanskrit: तीव्रमुत्पादितं दुःखं भ्रातृणां मे तथा पितुः। यथा सेयं नृशंसस्य कर्मणः फलमश्नुताम्॥
translation: This one has occasioned intense misery to my father and brothers Let her now take the fruit of her fell deed.

sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा च तेनाशु सखीजनसमावृता। गृहीता बलवत् कुब्जा सा तद् गृहमनादयत्॥
translation: Having said this, he furiously fell upon the hump backed one surrounded by her maids. Thereupon she with her cries made the chamber resound.

sanskrit: ततः सुभृशसंतप्तस्तस्याः सर्वः सखीजनः। क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय शत्रुघ्नं व्यपलायत सर्वशः॥
translation: Concluding Śatrughna fired with rage, her associates extremely pained, fled away in all directions.

sanskrit: अमन्त्रयत कृत्स्नश्च तस्याः सर्वः सखीजनः। यथायं समुपक्रान्तो निःशेष नः करिष्यति॥
translation: Then her companions in a body took counsel of each other, saying, “considering the way in which he has entered upon it, he will annihilate us quite."

sanskrit: सानुक्रोशां वदान्यां च धर्मज्ञां च यशस्विनीम्। कौसल्यां शरणं यामः सा हि नोऽस्ति ध्रुवा गतिः।।१५
translation: Let us therefore seek the protection of the tender hearted generous, pious and illustrious Kausalyā. Even she is our sure refuge.

sanskrit: सच रोषेण संवीतः शत्रुघ्नः शत्रुशासनः। विचकर्ष तदा कुब्जां क्रोशन्तीं पृथिवीतले॥
translation: Overpowered with rage, that chastiser of foes, Śatrughna, dragged the shrieking hump backed one to the ground.

sanskrit: तस्यां ह्याकृष्यमाणायां मन्थरायां ततस्ततः। चित्रं बहुविधं भाण्डं पृथिव्यां तद्व्यशीर्यत ॥
translation: As Mantharā was pushed this way and that, her various ornaments were scattered over the floor.

sanskrit: तेन भाण्डेन विस्तीर्णं श्रीमद् राजनिवेशनम्। अशोभत तदा भूयः शारदं गगनं यथा॥
translation: And strewn with those ornaments, the graceful chamber of the palace looked like the autumnal firmament.

sanskrit: स बली बलवत् क्रोधाद् गृहीत्वा पुरुषर्षभः। कैकेयीमभिनिर्भय बभाषे परुषं वचः॥
translation: And that foremost of men possessed of strength holding her, began to reprove Kaikeyī with harsh speech.

sanskrit: तैर्वाक्यैः परुषैर्दुःखैः कैकेयी भृशदुःखिता। शत्रुघ्नभयसंत्रस्ता पुत्रं शरणमागता॥
translation: Extremely hurt by those rough words, Kaikeyi terrified on account of Satrughna, took refuge with her son.

sanskrit: तं प्रेक्ष्य भरतः क्रुद्धं शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्। अवध्याः सर्वभूतानां प्रमदाः क्षम्यतामिति॥
translation: Thereupon casting his eyes on Satrughna, Bharata said, “A woman is incapable of being slain by any. Do you therefore excuse her.”

sanskrit: हन्यामहमिमां पापां कैकेयीं दुष्टचारिणीम्। यदि मां धार्मिको रामो नासूयेन्मातृघातकम्॥
translation: I myself would have slain this wicked Kaikeyi of impious deeds, if the righteous Rāma should not be displeased with me on account of my slaying my mother.

sanskrit: इमामपि हतां कुब्जां यदि जानाति राघवः। त्वां च मां चैव धर्मात्मा नाभिभाषिष्यते ध्रुवम्॥
translation: If Rāghava knows that the hump-backed one has been slain, he sure' will speak neither with you nor me.

sanskrit: भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणानुजः। न्यवर्तत ततो दोषात् तां मुमोच च मूर्च्छिताम्॥
translation: Hearing Bharata's words, Satrughna, younger brother to Lakşmaņa, refrained from that wrong and set free the hump-backed woman in a swoon.

sanskrit: सा पादमूले कैकेय्या मन्थरा निपपात ह। निःश्वसन्ती सुदुःखार्ता कृपणं विललाप ह॥
translation: Thereat, sighing hard in exceeding grief, Mantharā flung herself and Kaikeyi's feet, weeping piteously.

sanskrit: शत्रुघ्नविक्षेपविमूढसंज्ञां समीक्ष्य कुब्जां भरतस्य माता। शनैः समाश्वासयदार्तरूपां कौचीं विलग्नामिव वीक्षमाणाम्॥
translation: Seeing the hump-backed one deprived of her senses in consequence of the pushing she had received at the hands of Satrughna, Bharata's mother consoled that distressed woman, who appeared like a Krauñci that had been entrapped.

sanskrit: ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसेऽथ चतुर्दशे। समेत्य राजकर्तारो भरतं वाक्यमब्रुवन्॥
translation: Then on the morning of the fourteenth day, the ministers of the king assembled addressed Bharata in the following words.

sanskrit: गतो दशरथः स्वर्गं यो नो गुरुतरो गुरुः। रामं प्रव्राज्य वै ज्येष्ठं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्॥ त्वमद्य भव नो राजा राजपुत्र महायशः। संगत्या नापराध्नोति राज्यमेतदनायकम्॥...
translation: Having exiled his eldest son and the exceedingly strong Lakşmaņa, Dasaratha who was the superior of our superiors has gone to heaven. Do you, therefore, O illustrious prince, become our king. Having been permitted by the king you will commit no fault (by doing so), as this kingdom is without a master.

sanskrit: आभिषेचनिकं सर्वमिदमादाय राघव। प्रतीक्षते त्वां स्वजनः श्रेणयश्च नृपात्मज ॥
translation: O Raghava, having procured all these necessaries for the installation, the counsellor and othe, as well as the citizens wait, О king's son.

sanskrit: राज्यं गृहाण भरत पितृपैतामहं ध्रुवम्। अभिषेचय चात्मानं पाहि चास्मान् नरर्षभ॥
translation: Do you, O Bharata, take charge of this secure kingdom bequeathed by your father and grandfather. Do you, O foremost of men, have yourself sprinkled, and rule over us.

sanskrit: आभिषेचनिकं भाण्डं कृत्वा सर्वं प्रदक्षणिम्। भरतस्तं जनं सर्वं प्रत्युवाच धृतव्रतः॥
translation: Thereupon, having gone round all the things procured for the sprinkling, Bharata from in his vows addressed those persons, saying.

sanskrit: ज्येष्ठस्य राजता नित्यमुचिता हि कुलस्य नः। नैवं भवन्तो मां वक्तुमर्हन्ति कुशला जनाः॥
translation: In our line it is ever fit for the first-born alone to perform the task of government. It does not behove you who are wise to say so to me.

sanskrit: रामः पूर्वो हि नो भ्राता भविष्यति महीपतिः। अहं त्वरण्ये वत्स्यामि वर्षाणि नव पञ्च च॥
translation: Certainly Rāma our eldest brother shall become the king; and I will abide in the forest for five all nine years.

sanskrit: युज्यतां महती सेना चतुरङ्गमहाबला। आनयिष्याम्यहं ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरं राघवं वनात्॥
translation: Do you array the grand and mighty my consisting of fourfold forces. I will bring back from the forest my eldest brother Rāghava.

sanskrit: आभिषेचनिकं चैव सर्वमेतदुपस्कृतम्। पुरस्कृत्य गमिष्यामि रामहेतोर्वनं प्रति॥ तत्रैव तं नरव्याघ्रमभिषिच्य पुरस्कृतम्। आनयिष्यामि वै रामं हव्यवाहमिवाध्वरात्॥
translation: And taking all these necessaries for the investiture in front, I will go in the direction of the forest for Rāma. And sprinkling that chief of men on the spot, I will placing him in our front, bring Rāma back, like to fire brought in from the sacrifice.

sanskrit: न सकामां करिष्यामि स्वामिमां मातृगन्धिनीम्। वने वत्स्याम्यहं दुर्गे रामो राजा भविष्यति॥
translation: I will never fulfil the desire of this lady proud of her son. I will inhabit the impracticable woods, and Rāma shall become the monarch.

sanskrit: क्रियतां शिल्पिभिः पन्थाः समानि विषमाणि च। रक्षिणश्चानुसंयातु पथि दुर्गविचारकाः॥
translation: Let workmen lay out level roads in uneven tracts; and let those men that are adepts in threading places difficult to pass through, follow us.

sanskrit: एवं सम्भाषमाणं तं रामहेतोपात्मजम्। प्रत्युवाच जनः सर्वः श्रीमद्वाक्यमनुत्तमम्॥
translation: When the prince had spoken thus in behalf of Rāma, all those persons answered him in these excellent words.

sanskrit: एवं ते भाषमाणस्य पद्मा श्रीरुपतिष्ठताम्। यस्त्वं ज्येष्ठे नृपसुते पृथिवीं दातुमिच्छसि ॥
translation: For saying this, may Lakşmi seated on the lotus remain at they side; inasmuch you wish to confer the earth on the eldest son of the monarch!

sanskrit: अनुत्तमं तद्वचनं नृपात्मजः प्रभाषितं संश्रवणे निशम्य च। प्रहर्षजास्तं प्रति बाष्पविन्दवो निपेतुरार्यानननेत्रसम्भवाः॥
translation: Hearing that graceful speech of the king's son, tear-drops. begot of delight began to trickle from their eyes and adorned those noble countenances.

sanskrit: ऊचुस्ते वचनमिदं निशम्य हृष्टाः सामात्याः सपरिषदो वियातशोकाः। पन्थानं नरवरभक्तिमान् जनश्च व्यादिष्टस्तव वचनाच्च शिल्पिवर्गः॥
translation: Their grief removed, with cheerful hearts, the counsellors, courtiers, and others hearing that speech (of the prince), said, “O best of men, according to your order artizans as well as people cherishing a high regard for you have been directed to lay out a read."

sanskrit: ततो नान्दीमुखीं रात्रि भरतं सूतमागधाः। तुष्टुवुः सविशेषज्ञाः स्तवैर्मङ्गलसंस्तवैः॥
translation: Then seeing that the night in which had been performed the auspicious preliminary ceremonies, was about to be spent, eulogists and genealogists hymned Bharata with consecrated hymns.

sanskrit: सुवर्णकोणाभिहतः प्राणदद्यामदुन्दुभिः। दध्मुः शङ्खांश्च शतशो वाद्यांश्चोच्चावचस्वरान्॥
